nodes.name: Approximation function psi
nodes.statement: Let $\psi:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{R}_{\geqslant0}$ be an arbitrary function from the positive integers to the non-negative reals.

nodes.name: Rational approximation inequality
nodes.statement: \bigg|\alpha-\frac{a}{q}\bigg| \leqslant \frac{\psi(q)}{q}.
nodes.label: eq:rational approximations

nodes.name: Lebesgue measure lambda
nodes.statement: To state his result, we let $\lambda$ denote the Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}$.
also_stated_at: We reserve the letter $\lambda$ for the Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}$.

nodes.name: Khinchin's theorem
nodes.statement: Consider a function $\psi:\mathbb{N}\to[0,+\infty)$ such that the sequence $(q\psi(q))_{q=1}^\infty$ is decreasing, and let $\mathcal{K}$ denote the set of real numbers $\alpha\in[0,1]$ for which \eqref{eq:rational approximations} has infinitely many solutions $(a,q)\in\mathbb{Z}^2$ with $0\leqslant a\leqslant q$. Then the following hold: \begin{enumerate} \item If $\sum_{q\geqslant1} \psi(q)<\infty$, then $\lambda(\mathcal{K})=0$. \item If $\sum_{q\geqslant1} \psi(q)=\infty$, then $\lambda(\mathcal{K})=1$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: For decreasing $q\psi(q)$, the set of $\psi$-approximable reals has measure 0 or 1 according as $\sum\psi(q)$ converges or diverges.
assumptions: $\psi:\mathbb{N}\to[0,+\infty)$ such that the sequence $(q\psi(q))_{q=1}^\infty$ is decreasing

nodes.name: Sets K_q
nodes.statement: Consider the sets \eq{ \mathcal{K}_q= [0,1]\cap \bigcup_{a=0}^q \Big[\frac{a-\psi(q)}{q}, \frac{a+\psi(q)}{q}\Big] , } so that\footnote{Recall that if $X_1,X_2,\dots$ is a sequence of sets of real numbers, then $\limsup_{n\to\infty}X_n$ denotes the set of real numbers lying in infinitely many $X_n$'s.} \[ \mathcal{K} =\limsup_{q\to\infty}\mathcal{K}_q. \]
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal{K}_q$ is the union of intervals of radius $\psi(q)/q$ around $a/q$ in $[0,1]$, so $\mathcal{K}=\limsup\mathcal{K}_q$.

nodes.name: Definition of K_q
nodes.statement: \mathcal{K}_q= [0,1]\cap \bigcup_{a=0}^q \Big[\frac{a-\psi(q)}{q}, \frac{a+\psi(q)}{q}\Big] ,

nodes.name: Borel-Cantelli heuristic for Khinchin's theorem
nodes.statement: In addition, \[ \min\{\psi(q),1/2\}\leqslant \lambda(\mathcal{K}_q)\leqslant 2\min\{\psi(q),1/2\}. \] Thus, part (a) of Khinchin's theorem is an immediate corollary of the `easy' direction of the Borel-Cantelli lemma from Probability Theory \cite[Lemma 1.2]{harman} applied to the probability space $[0,1]$ equipped with the measure $\lambda$. If we knew, in addition, that the sets $\mathcal{K}_q$ were mutually independent, then we could apply the `hard' direction of the Borel-Cantelli lemma \cite[Lemma 1.3]{harman} to deduce part (b) of Khinchin's theorem. Of course, the sets $\mathcal{K}_q$ are not mutually independent, so the difficulty in Khinchin's proof is showing that there is enough `approximate independence', so that $\mathcal{K}$ still has full measure.
nodes.statement_short: Since $\lambda(\mathcal{K}_q)\asymp\min\{\psi(q),1/2\}$, part (a) follows from Borel-Cantelli; part (b) needs approximate independence of the $\mathcal{K}_q$.

nodes.name: Sets A_q and A (reduced approximations)
nodes.statement: To this end, let \begin{equation} \mathcal{A}_q:= [0,1]\cap \bigcup_{\substack{1\leqslant a\leqslant q \\ \gcd(a,q)=1}} \Big[\frac{a-\psi(q)}{q}, \frac{a+\psi(q)}{q}\Big] . \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \mathcal{A}:= \limsup_{q\to\infty} \mathcal{A}_q. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal{A}_q$: union of intervals of radius $\psi(q)/q$ around reduced fractions $a/q$; $\mathcal{A}=\limsup\mathcal{A}_q$.

nodes.name: Definition of A_q
nodes.statement: \mathcal{A}_q:= [0,1]\cap \bigcup_{\substack{1\leqslant a\leqslant q \\ \gcd(a,q)=1}} \Big[\frac{a-\psi(q)}{q}, \frac{a+\psi(q)}{q}\Big] .
nodes.label: eq:A_q-dfn

nodes.name: Definition of A
nodes.statement: \mathcal{A}:= \limsup_{q\to\infty} \mathcal{A}_q.
nodes.label: eq:A-dfn

nodes.name: Convergence half of the Duffin-Schaeffer problem
nodes.statement: \sum_{q=1}^\infty \frac{\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q}<\infty \qquad\implies\qquad \lambda(\mathcal{A})=0.
nodes.label: DS-BC

nodes.name: Duffin-Schaeffer conjecture
nodes.statement: \sum_{q=1}^\infty \frac{\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q}=\infty \qquad\implies\qquad \lambda(\mathcal{A})=1.
nodes.statement_short: Divergence of $\sum\varphi(q)\psi(q)/q$ implies that almost every $\alpha$ has infinitely many reduced approximations $|\alpha-a/q|\le\psi(q)/q$.
nodes.label: DS-conj

nodes.name: Duffin-Schaeffer theorem
nodes.statement: Let $\psi:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow \mathbb{R}_{\geqslant 0}$ be a function such that \[ \sum_{q=1}^\infty \frac{\psi(q)\varphi(q)}{q}=\infty. \] Let $\mathcal{A}$ be the set of $\alpha\in[0,1]$ for which the inequality \eq{ \bigg|\alpha-\frac{a}{q}\bigg| \leqslant \frac{\psi(q)}{q} } has infinitely many coprime solutions $a$ and $q$. Then $\mathcal{A}$ has Lebesgue measure 1.
nodes.statement_short: If $\sum\psi(q)\varphi(q)/q=\infty$, almost all $\alpha\in[0,1]$ have infinitely many coprime solutions to $|\alpha-a/q|\le\psi(q)/q$.
nodes.label: thm:MainThm

nodes.name: Rational approximation inequality (restated in Theorem 1)
nodes.statement: \bigg|\alpha-\frac{a

nodes.name: Catlin's conjecture
nodes.statement: Let $\psi:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow \mathbb{R}_{\geqslant 0}$ and let $\mathcal{K}$ denote the set of $\alpha\in[0,1]$ for which the inequality \eqref{eq:rational approximations again} has infinitely many solutions $(a,q)\in\mathbb{Z}^2$ with $0\leqslant a\leqslant q$. Define $\psi^*:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}_{\geqslant 0}$ by \[ \psi^*(q):=\varphi(q)\sup\{\psi(n)/n \,:\, n\in\mathbb{N},\ q|n\} . \] Then the following hold: \begin{enumerate}[topsep=2pt, itemsep=2pt] \item If $\sum_{q=1}^\infty \psi^*(q)<\infty$, then $\lambda(\mathcal{K})=0$. \item If $\sum_{q=1}^\infty \psi^*(q)=\infty$, then $\lambda(\mathcal{K})=1$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Khinchin-type zero-one law for non-reduced approximations without monotonicity, governed by $\psi^*(q)=\varphi(q)\sup_{q|n}\psi(n)/n$.
nodes.label: thm:catlin

nodes.name: Walfisz's observation (monotone case of Duffin-Schaeffer)
nodes.statement: Thus, as observed by Walfisz \cite{walfisz} (in work predating Duffin and Schaeffer's conjecture), Khinchin's Theorem implies the Duffin-Schaeffer conjecture when $q\psi(q)$ is decreasing.
conclusions: Khinchin's Theorem implies the Duffin-Schaeffer conjecture

nodes.name: Walfisz's strengthening of Khinchin's theorem
nodes.statement: In the same paper, he strengthened part (b) of Khinchin's theorem as follows: if $\sum_{q\geqslant1}\psi(q)=\infty$ and $\psi(q)\ll\psi(2q)$ for all $q\in\mathbb{N}$, then the set of $\alpha\in[0,1]$ for which \eqref{eq:rational approximations} has infinitely many coprime solutions $a$ and $q$ has Lebesgue measure 1.
conclusions: the set of $\alpha\in[0,1]$ for which \eqref{eq:rational approximations} has infinitely many coprime solutions $a$ and $q$ has Lebesgue measure 1

nodes.name: Duffin-Schaeffer theorem for regular psi
nodes.statement: More precisely, they proved \eqref{DS-conj} under the assumption that \[ \limsup_{Q\to\infty} \frac{\sum_{q\leqslant Q}\psi(q)\varphi(q)/q}{\sum_{q\leqslant Q}\psi(q)}>0 . \]

nodes.name: Erdos-Vaaler theorem
nodes.statement: The first significant step was achieved by Erd\H os \cite{erdos} and then improved by Vaaler \cite{vaaler}, who demonstrated \eqref{DS-conj} when $\psi(q)=O(1/q)$.

nodes.name: Pollington-Vaughan theorem (higher-dimensional Duffin-Schaeffer)
nodes.statement: In addition, Pollington and Vaughan \cite{PV} proved that the $d$-dimensional analogue of the Duffin-Schaeffer conjecture holds for any $d\geqslant2$.
conclusions: the $d$-dimensional analogue of the Duffin-Schaeffer conjecture holds

nodes.name: Duffin-Schaeffer with extra divergence (Aistleitner-Lachmann-Munsch-Technau-Zafeiropoulos)
nodes.statement: The strongest published such result is the recent theorem of Aistleitner, Lachmann, Munsch, Technau and Zafeiropoulos \cite{aistleitner} who showed that \eq{ \sum_{q=1}^\infty \frac{\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q(\log{q})^\varepsilon}=\infty \qquad\implies\qquad \lambda(\mathcal{A})=1, } for any fixed $\varepsilon>0$.

nodes.name: Extra divergence implication
nodes.statement: \sum_{q=1}^\infty \frac{\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q(\log{q})^\varepsilon}=\infty \qquad\implies\qquad \lambda(\mathcal{A})=1,

nodes.name: Aistleitner's slow divergence theorem
nodes.statement: In 2014, Aistleitner \cite{aistleiner} established a companion result to the above one: he showed that if $\sum_{q=1}^\infty\psi(q)\varphi(q)/q$ diverges and $\psi$ is not `too concentrated', in the sense that \eq{ \sum_{ 2^{2^j}<q\leqslant 2^{2^{j+1}} } \frac{\psi(q)\varphi(q)}{q}=O(1/j)\qquad \text{for all}\quad j\geqslant1 , } then $\lambda(\mathcal{A})=1$.

nodes.name: Slow divergence condition
nodes.statement: \sum_{ 2^{2^j}<q\leqslant 2^{2^{j+1}} } \frac{\psi(q)\varphi(q)}{q}=O(1/j)\qquad \text{for all}\quad j\geqslant1 ,

nodes.name: Aistleitner's decoupling improvement
nodes.statement: In the recent progress report \cite{aistleitner2}, Aistleitner explains how to improve on \eqref{extra divergence} and \eqref{slow divergence}. In particular, his refined arguments allow him to replace $(\log q)^\varepsilon$ by $(\log\log q)^\varepsilon$ in \eqref{extra divergence}.

nodes.name: Deduction of the Hausdorff dimension corollary
nodes.statement: Finally, Beresnevich and Velani \cite{hausdorff DS} have proven that the Duffin-Schaeffer conjecture implies a Hausdorff measure version of itself. An immediate corollary of their results when combined with Theorem \ref{thm:MainThm} is the following.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the Beresnevich-Velani mass transference principle with Theorem 1.

nodes.name: Hausdorff dimension of the Duffin-Schaeffer set
nodes.statement: Let $\psi:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow [0,1/2]$. Write $\mathcal{A}$ for the set of $\alpha\in[0,1]$ such that \eqref{eq:rational approximations again} has infinitely many coprime solutions $a$ and $q$, and set \[ s=\inf\Bigl\{\beta\in\mathbb{R}_{\geqslant 0}:\,\sum_{q=1}^\infty \varphi(q)(\psi(q)/q)^\beta<\infty\Bigl\}. \] Then the Hausdorff dimension $\dim_{\mathcal{H}}(\mathcal{A})$ of $\mathcal{A}$ satisfies \[ \dim_{\mathcal{H}}(\mathcal{A})=\min(s,1). \]
nodes.statement_short: For $\psi\le1/2$, $\dim_{\mathcal{H}}\mathcal{A}=\min(s,1)$ with $s$ the convergence exponent of $\sum\varphi(q)(\psi(q)/q)^\beta$.

nodes.name: Generic measure mu
nodes.statement: The letter $\mu$ will always denote a generic measure on $\mathbb{N}$.

nodes.name: Bipartite graph triple
nodes.statement: A triple $G=(\mathcal{V},\mathcal{W},\mathcal{E})$ denotes a bipartite graph with vertex sets $\mathcal{V}$ and $\mathcal{W}$ and edge set $\mathcal{E}\subseteq\mathcal{V}\times\mathcal{W}$.

nodes.name: Indicator function
nodes.statement: Given a set or an event $\mathcal{E}$, we let $\mathds{1}_{\mathcal{E}}$ denote its indicator function.

nodes.name: Exact prime power divisibility
nodes.statement: We also write $p^k\|n$ to mean that $p^k$ is the exact power of $p$ dividing the integer $n$.

nodes.name: gcd and lcm notation
nodes.statement: In contrast, we write $\gcd(a,b)$ for the greatest common divisor of the integers $a$ and $b$ and $\mathrm{lcm}(a,b)$ for the least common multiple of $a$ and $b$.

nodes.name: Vinogradov notation
nodes.statement: Finally, we adopt the usual asymptotic notation of Vinogradov: given two functions $f,g:X\to\mathbb{R}$ and a set $Y\subseteq X$, we write ``$f(x)\ll g(x)$ for all $x\in Y$'' if there is a constant $c=c(f,g,Y)>0$ such that $|f(x)|\leqslant cg(x)$ for all $x\in Y$.

nodes.name: Landau notation
nodes.statement: If $h:X\to\mathbb{R}$ is a third function, we use Landau's notation ``$f=g+O(h)$ on $Y$'' to mean that $|f-g|\ll h$ on $Y$.

nodes.name: Deduction of Catlin's conjecture from Theorem 1
nodes.statement: Most of the details of this deduction can be found in Catlin's original paper \cite{catlin}. We give them here as well for the sake of completeness. For easy reference, let \[ S=\sum_{q=1}^\infty \varphi(q)\sup_{\substack{n\in\mathbb{N}\\ q|n}} \frac{\psi(n)}{n} . \] Firstly, we deal with a rather trivial case. \bigskip \noindent {\it Case 1:} There is a sequence of integers $q_1<q_2<\cdots$ such that $\psi(q_i)\geqslant1/2$ for all $i$. \medskip By passing to a subsequence if necessary, we may assume that $q_{i+1}\geqslant 2q_i^2$ for all $i$. Recall the definition of the set $\mathcal{K}_q$ from \eqref{def:K_q}. Since $\psi(q_i)\geqslant1/2$, we infer that $\mathcal{K}_{q_i}=[0,1]$ for each $i$. As a consequence, $\mathcal{K}=[0,1]$. We claim that we also have $S=\infty$. Indeed, for each $d|q_i$, we have \[ \sup_{\substack{n\in\mathbb{N}\\ d|n}} \frac{\psi(n)}{n}\geqslant \frac{\psi(q_i)}{q_i}\geqslant\frac{1}{2q_i}. \] Consequently, \eq{ \sum_{q_{i-1}<q\leqslant q_i} \varphi(q)\sup_{\substack{n\in\mathbb{N}\\ q|n}} \frac{\psi(n)}{n} \geqslant \sum_{\substack{q_{i-1}<q\leqslant q_i\\ q|q_i}} \frac{\varphi(q)}{2q_i}\geqslant \frac{1}{2q_i}\sum_{q|q_i}\varphi(q)-\frac{1}{2q_i}\sum_{q\leqslant q_{i-1}}\varphi(q)\geqslant \frac{1}{4}, } since $\sum_{q|q_i}\varphi(q)=q_i$ and $\sum_{q\leqslant q_{i-1}}\varphi(q)\leqslant q_{i-1}^2\leqslant q_i/2$. Summing \eqref{eq:catlin1} over all $i\geqslant2$ proves our claim that $S=\infty$. Hence, if we are in Case 1, we see that $S=\infty$ and $\mathcal{K}=[0,1]$, so that Theorem \ref{thm:catlin} holds. \bigskip \noindent {\it Case 2:} There are finitely many $q\in\mathbb{N}$ with $\psi(q)\geqslant1/2$. \medskip Note that in this case replacing $\psi$ by $\min\{\psi,1/2\}$ does not affect either the convergence of $S$, nor which numbers lie in the set $\mathcal{K}=\limsup_{q\to\infty}\mathcal{K}_q$. Hence, we may assume without loss of generality that $\psi\leqslant1/2$. In particular, we have that $\lim_{n\to\infty}\psi(n)/n=0$, so that we may replace $\sup$ by $\max$ in the definition of $S$. We now follow an argument due to Catlin. Consider the function $\xi$ defined by \[ \frac{\xi(q)}{q}=\max_{\substack{n\in\mathbb{N}\\ q|n}} \frac{\psi(n)}{n} \] and the sets \[ \mathcal{C}_q= [0,1]\cap \bigcup_{\substack{1\leqslant a\leqslant q \\ \gcd(a,q)=1}} \Big[\frac{a-\xi(q)}{q}, \frac{a+\xi(q)}{q}\Big] \qquad\text{and}\qquad \mathcal{C}:= \limsup_{q\to\infty} \mathcal{C}_q . \] These are the analogues of the sets $\mathcal{A}_q$ and $\mathcal{A}$ that appear in Theorem \ref{thm:MainThm}, but with $\xi$ in place of $\psi$. We claim that \eq{ \mathcal{C}\setminus\mathbb{Q}=\mathcal{K}\setminus\mathbb{Q}. } This will immediately complete the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:catlin}(b) by applying Theorem \ref{thm:MainThm}. In addition, Theorem \ref{thm:catlin}(a) will follow from \eqref{DS-BC}. Indeed, if $\alpha \in \mathcal{C}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$, then there are infinitely many reduced fractions $a_j/q_j$ such $|\alpha-a_j/q_j|\leqslant\xi(q_j)/q_j$. By the definition of $\xi$, there is some $n_j$ that is a multiple of $q_j$ such that $\xi(q_j)/q_j=\psi(n_j)/n_j$. If we let $m_j=a_j n_j/q_j$, then $|\alpha-m_j/n_j|\leqslant \psi(n_j)/n_j$ for all $j$. Since $\lim_{j\to\infty}q_j=\infty$ and $n_j\geqslant q_j$ for each $j$, we also have that $\lim_{j\to\infty}n_j=\infty$, whence $\alpha \in \mathcal{K}$. Conversely, let $\alpha \in \mathcal{K}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$. Then there are infinitely many pairs $(m_j,n_j)\in\mathbb{N}^2$ such that $|\alpha-m_j/n_j|\leqslant\psi(n_j)/n_j$. If we let $a_j/q_j$ be the fraction $m_j/n_j$ in reduced form, we also have that $|\alpha-a_j/q_j|\leqslant\psi(n_j)/n_j\leqslant \xi(q_j)/q_j$, where the last inequality follows by noticing that $q_j|n_j$. This shows that $\alpha\in \mathcal{C}$, as long as we can show that infinitely many of the fractions $a_j/q_j$ are distinct. But if this were not the case, there would exist a fraction $a/q$ such that $a_j/q_j=a/q$ for infinitely many $j$, so that $|\alpha-a/q|\leqslant \psi(n_j)/n_j\leqslant1/(2n_j)$ for all such $j$. Letting $j\to\infty$, we find that $\alpha=a/q\in\mathbb{Q}$, a contradiction. This completes the proof of \eqref{eq:catlin2}, and hence of Theorem \ref{thm:catlin} in all cases.
nodes.statement_short: Case analysis on whether $\psi\ge1/2$ infinitely often; otherwise Catlin's argument shows $\mathcal{C}\setminus\mathbb{Q}=\mathcal{K}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$ for $\xi(q)/q=\max_{q|n}\psi(n)/n$, then apply Theorem 1.

nodes.statement: \mathcal{C}\setminus\mathbb{Q}=\mathcal{K}\setminus\mathbb{Q}.

nodes.name: Outline of the proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: The purpose of this section is to explain in rough terms the main ideas that go into the proof of our main result. To simplify various technicalities, let us consider the special case where the function $\psi$ satisfies the following conditions: \begin{enumerate} \item $\psi(q)=0$ or $\psi(q)=q^{-c}$ for every $q\in\mathbb{N}$\,; \item $\psi$ is non-zero only on square-free integers $q$\,; \item There exists an infinite sequence $2<x_1<x_2<\dots$ such that: \begin{enumerate} \item $x_j>x_{j-1}^2$\,; \item $\psi$ is supported on $\cup_{i=1}^{\infty}[x_i,2x_i]$\,; \item for each $i$ we have \[ \sum_{q\in [x_i,2x_i]}\frac{\varphi(q)}{q}\psi(q)\in[1,2] \,. \] \end{enumerate} \end{enumerate} In this set-up, it follows from a well-known second moment argument (which will be explained in detail in Section \ref{sec:Prelim}) that to establish the Duffin-Schaeffer conjecture it is sufficient to show that for any $x\in \{x_1,\,x_2,\dots\}$ we have \[ \sum_{\substack{q,r\in\mathcal{S}\\\gcd(q,r)\leqslant M(q,r)}}\frac{\varphi(q)}{q}\cdot \frac{\varphi(r)}{r}\cdot P(q,r)\ll x^{2c}, \] where \begin{align*} \mathcal{S}&:=\{q\in\mathbb{Z}\cap[x,2x] : \psi(q)\neq0\},\\ M(q,r)&:=\max\{q\psi(r),r\psi(q)\}\asymp x^{1-c},\\ P(q,r)&:=\prod_{\substack{p|qr/\gcd(q,r)^2\\ p>M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)}}\Bigl(1+\frac{1}{p}\Bigr). \end{align*} Note that we have the estimate \[ \sum_{q\in \mathcal{S}}\frac{\varphi(q)}{q}\asymp x^{c}\sum_{q\in\mathcal{S}}\frac{\varphi(q)}{q}\psi(q)\asymp x^{c} , \] so the key to the proof is to show that $P(q,r)\ll 1$ on average over $q,r\in\mathcal{S}$. This would then show suitable `approximate independence' of the sets $\mathcal{A}_q$ defined by \eqref{eq:A_q-dfn}. The size of $P(q,r)$ is controlled by small primes dividing exactly one of $q,r$. With this in mind, let us consider separately the contribution from $q,r$ with \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{p|qr/\gcd(q,r)^2\\ p\geqslant t}}\frac{1}{p}\approx 1 \end{equation} for different thresholds $t$ (which we think of as small compared with $x$). A calculation then shows that it is sufficient to show that for each $t\geqslant1$ \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{q,r\in\mathcal{S} \\ \gcd(q,r)\geqslant x^{1-c}/t}}\frac{\varphi(q)}{q}\cdot \frac{\varphi(r)}{r}\ll \frac{x^{2c}}{t}. \end{equation} In particular, we need to understand the structure of a set $\mathcal{S}$ where many of the pairs $(q,r)\in\mathcal{S}^2$ have a large common factor. There are $O(x^c)$ choices of $q\in \mathcal{S}$ weighted by $\varphi(q)/q$. Given $q\in \mathcal{S}$, there are $x^{o(1)}$ divisors of $q$ that are at least $x^{1-c}/t$. In turn, given such a divisor $d$, there are $O(x^c t)$ integers $r\in[x,2x]$ which are a multiple of $d$ (forgetting the constraint $r\in\mathcal{S}$). This gives a bound $t x^{2c+o(1)}$ for the sum in \eqref{eq:jSum}, and so the key problem is to win back a little bit more than the $x^{o(1)}$ factor from the divisor bound. We wish to do this by gaining a structural understanding of sets $\mathcal{S}$ where many pairs have a large GCD. One way that many pairs in $\mathcal{S}$ can have a large GCD is if a positive proportion of elements of $\mathcal{S}$ are a multiple of some fixed divisor $d$. It is natural to ask if this is the only such construction. If we ignore the $\varphi(q)/q$ weights, this leads us to the following prototypical question that we shall refer to as the {\it Model Problem}. \begin{ModelProblem} Let $\mathcal{S}\subseteq[x,2x]$ satisfy $\#\mathcal{S}\asymp x^{c}$ and be such that there are $\#\mathcal{S}^2/100$ pairs $(a_1,a_2)\in\mathcal{S}^2$ with $\gcd(a_1,a_2)>x^{1-c}$. Must it be the case that there is an integer $d\gg x^{1-c}$ which divides $\gg \#\mathcal{S}$ elements of $\mathcal{S}$? \end{ModelProblem} It turns out that the answer to this Model Problem as stated is `no', but a technical variant of it that is sufficient for proving Theorem \ref{thm:MainThm} has a positive answer. For the purposes of this section, we will ignore this subtle issue; we will return to it and discuss it in detail in Section \ref{sec:Concluding}. \medskip To attack our Model Problem, we use a `compression' argument, roughly inspired by the papers of Erd\H os-Ko-Rado \cite{erdoskorado} and Dyson \cite{dyson}. We will repeatedly pass to subsets of $\mathcal{S}$ where we have increasing control over whether given primes occur in the GCDs or not, whilst at the same time showing that the size of the original set is controlled in terms of the size of the new set. At the end of the iteration procedure we will then have arrived at a subset which controls the size of $\mathcal{S}$, and where we know that all large GCDs are caused by a fixed divisor. Since the final set then has a very simple GCD structure, we will have enough information to establish \eqref{eq:jSum}. To enable the iterations, we pass to a bipartite setup. We start out with sets $\mathcal{V}_0=\mathcal{W}_0=\mathcal{S}$. Then, we construct two decreasing sequences of sets $\mathcal{V}_0\supset \mathcal{V}_1\supset\mathcal{V}_2\supset \cdots$ and $\mathcal{W}_0\supset\mathcal{W}_1\supset\mathcal{W}_2\supset \cdots$, as well as a sequence of primes $p_1,p_2,\dots$ such that either $p_j$ divides all elements of $\mathcal{V}_j$, or $p_j$ is coprime to all elements of $\mathcal{V}_j$ (and similarly with $\mathcal{W}_j$). Since $\mathcal{S}$ contains only square-free integers in the simplified set-up of this section, this means that there will be exponents $k_j,\ell_j\in\{0,1\}$ such that $p_j^{k_j}\|v$ for all $v\in\mathcal{V}_j$, and $p_j^{\ell_j}\|w$ for all $w\in\mathcal{W}_j$. Hence, if we let $a_j=p_1^{k_1}\cdots p_j^{k_j}$ and $b_j=p_1^{\ell_1}\cdots p_j^{\ell_j}$, then $a_j$ will divide all elements of $\mathcal{W}_j$ and $b_j$ will divide all elements of $\mathcal{V}_j$. We will construct the sets $\mathcal{V}_1,\mathcal{V}_2,\dots$ and $\mathcal{W}_1,\mathcal{W}_2,\dots$ in an iterative fashion. Assume that after $j$ iterations we have arrived at the sets $\mathcal{V}_j,\mathcal{W}_j\subseteq\mathcal{S}$. We then pick a prime $p_{j+1}$ that is different from $p_1,\dots,p_j$, and that occurs as the prime factor of $\gcd(v,w)$ for some $v\in\mathcal{V}_j$, $w\in\mathcal{W}_j$ with $\gcd(v,w)>x^{1-c}/t$. Our goal is to pass judiciously to subsets $\mathcal{V}_{j+1}\subseteq\mathcal{V}_j$ and $\mathcal{W}_{j+1}\subseteq\mathcal{W}_j$ where either $\mathcal{V}_{j+1}$ is all elements of $\mathcal{V}_j$ that are divisible by $p_{j+1}$, or $\mathcal{V}_{j+1}$ is all elements of $\mathcal{V}_j$ coprime to $p_{j+1}$ (and similarly with $\mathcal{W}_{j+1}$). Since we're assuming that $\mathcal{S}$ contains only square-free integers, we then will completely know the $p_{j+1}$-divisibility of all elements of $\mathcal{V}_{j+1}$ and $\mathcal{W}_{j+1}$, so in particular all GCDs between an element of $\mathcal{V}_{j+1}$ and $\mathcal{W}_{j+1}$ will either be multiple of $p_{j+1}$, or all will be coprime to $p_{j+1}$. Eventually, we will arrive at a pair of sets $(\mathcal{V}_J,\mathcal{W}_J)$ such that every pair $(v,w)\in\mathcal{V}_J\times\mathcal{W}_J$ with $\gcd(v,w)>x^{1-c}/t$ has the property that all prime factors of $\gcd(v,w)$ will lie in the set $\{p_1,\dots,p_J\}$ (and moreover we will ensure that there is at least one such pair). This terminates the iterative procedure. By construction, all elements of $\mathcal{V}=\mathcal{V}_J$ will be divisible by the fixed integer $a=a_J$, and similarly all elements of $\mathcal{W}=\mathcal{W}_J$ will be divisible by the fixed integer $b=b_J$. In addition, if $v\in\mathcal{V}$ and $w\in\mathcal{W}$ has $\gcd(v,w)>x^{1-c}/t$, then in fact $\gcd(v,w)$ will be exactly equal to $\gcd(a,b)$ since we know the $p_j$-divisibility for all elements of $\mathcal{V}$ and $\mathcal{W}$. Thus, $\gcd(a,b)>x^{1-c}/t$ and actually every pair $v\in \mathcal{V}$ and $w\in\mathcal{W}$ has $\gcd(v,w)=\gcd(a,b)$. Naturally, the success of the above strategy depends on improving the `structure' of the pair of sets $(\mathcal{V}_j,\mathcal{W}_j)$ at each stage of the algorithm. This will enable us to control a quantity like the left hand side of \eqref{eq:jSum} in terms of a related quantity for $(\mathcal{V},\mathcal{W})=(\mathcal{V}_J,\mathcal{W}_J)$. An initially appealing choice to measure the `structure' might be \[ \delta_j=\frac{\#\{(v,w)\in\mathcal{V}_j\times\mathcal{W}_j:\, \gcd(v,w)>x^{1-c}/t\}}{\#\mathcal{V}_j\cdot \#\mathcal{W}_j}, \] namely the density of pairs $(v,w)$ with large GCD at stage $j$. Iteratively increasing this quantity would try to mimic a `density increment' strategy such as that used in the proof of Roth's Theorem on arithmetic progressions \cite{roth1,roth2}. Unfortunately, such an argument loses all control over the size of the sets $\mathcal{V}_j,\mathcal{W}_j$, and so we lose control over the sum in \eqref{eq:jSum}. An alternative suggestion might be to consider a different quantity which focuses on the size of the sets. Recall that all elements of $\mathcal{V}_j$ are a multiple of $a_j$, all elements of $\mathcal{W}_j$ are a multiple of $b_j$, and that in our final step we have $\gcd(a,b)>x^{1-c}/t$. Thus \al{ \#\mathcal{V}\cdot \#\mathcal{W} &\leqslant \#\{(v,w)\in(\mathbb{Z}\cap[x,2x])^2 : a|v,\ b|w\} \ll \frac{x^2}{ab} \leqslant t^2 x^{2c}\cdot \frac{\gcd(a,b)^2}{ab} , } where we used that $\mathcal{V}=\mathcal{V}_J$ and $\mathcal{W}=\mathcal{W}_J$ are subsets of $[x,2x]$ in \eqref{eq:anatomy2}. Thus, one might try to iteratively increase the quantity \[ \#\mathcal{V}_j\cdot \#\mathcal{W}_j\cdot \frac{a_jb_j}{\gcd(a_j,b_j)^2}. \] This would adequately control \eqref{eq:jSum}, but unfortunately it is not possible to guarantee that this quantity increases at each stage, and so this proposal also fails. However, the variant \begin{equation} \delta_j^{10}\cdot \#\mathcal{V}_j\cdot \#\mathcal{W}_j \cdot\frac{a_jb_j}{\gcd(a_j,b_j)^2} \end{equation} turns out to (more-or-less) work well. Indeed, if the quantity \eqref{eq:QualityAttempt} increases at each iteration, and at the final iteration all elements of $\mathcal{V}=\mathcal{V}_J$ are a multiple of $a=a_J$, all elements of $\mathcal{W}=\mathcal{W}_J$ are a multiple of $b=b_J$, and all edges come from pairs $(v,w)$ with $\gcd(v,w)=\gcd(a,b)>x^{1-c}/t$, then we find that \begin{equation} \delta_0^{10}\cdot \#\mathcal{S}^2\leqslant \delta_J^{10}\cdot \#\mathcal{V}\cdot \#\mathcal{W}\cdot \frac{ab}{\gcd(a,b)^2} \leqslant \#\mathcal{V}\cdot \#\mathcal{W} \cdot \frac{ab}{\gcd(a,b)^2}\ll t^2x^{2c}. \end{equation} We note that in our setup $\#\mathcal{S}\asymp x^{c}$, and that \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{q,r\in\mathcal{S} \\ \gcd(q,r)>x^{1-c}/t}}1=\delta_0\cdot \#\mathcal{S}^2. \end{equation} If it so happens that $\delta_0\leqslant 1/t$, then we trivially obtain \eqref{eq:jSum} (ignoring the $\varphi(q)/q$ weighting) from \eqref{eq:EdgeRewrite}. On the other hand, if $\delta_0\gg 1/t $, then \eqref{eq:IterationBound1} falls short of \eqref{eq:jSum} only by a factor $t^{12}$. Finally, to win the additional factor of $t^{12}$ we make use of the fact that any edge $(q,r)$ in our graph satisfies \eqref{eq:tThreshold}. The crucial estimate is that \eq{ \#\Bigl\{n<x:\sum_{\substack{p|n\\ p\geqslant t}}\frac{1}{p}\geqslant 1\Bigr\}\ll e^{-t} x . } This was the key idea in the earlier work of Erd\H os \cite{erdos} and Vaaler \cite{vaaler} on the Duffin-Schaeffer conjecture. In our case, our iteration procedure has essentially reduced the proof to a similar situation to their work. Indeed, in \eqref{eq:anatomy2}, we may restrict our attention to pairs $(v,w)$ such that $a|v$, $b|w$ and \eq{ \sum_{\substack{p|vw/\gcd(v,w)^2 \\ p\geqslant t}} \frac{1}{p} \approx 1. } Unless most of the contribution to the above sum of comes from primes in $a$ and $b$, we can apply \eqref{eq:anatomy-gain} to win a factor of size $e^{-t}=o(t^{-12})$ in \eqref{eq:anatomy2}. Finally, if the small primes in $a$ and $b$ do cause a problem, then a more careful analysis of our iteration procedure shows that we actually are able to increase the quantity \eqref{eq:QualityAttempt} by more than $t^{12}$ by the final stage $J$, which also suffices for establishing \eqref{eq:jSum} in this case. \medskip The above description has ignored several important technicalities; it turns out that the $\varphi(q)/q$ weights are vital for our argument to work (see the discussion in Section \ref{sec:Concluding}). In addition, we do not quite work with \eqref{eq:QualityAttempt} but with a closely related (but more complicated) expression to enable this quantity to increase at each iteration. The iteration procedure of our argument is broken up into different stages. In between two of the principal iterative stages, we perform a certain `clean-up' step at which we allow a small loss in the quantity \eqref{eq:QualityAttempt}. This step is essential in order to keep track of the condition \eqref{eq:anatomy-condition-rough} (which could otherwise become meaningless after too many iterations).
nodes.section: 3 Outline of the proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement_short: Heuristic sketch: reduce to a GCD-pair sum bound, then a compression/density-increment iteration on a quality $\delta^{10}\#\mathcal{V}\#\mathcal{W}ab/\gcd(a,b)^2$. Anatomy-of-integers estimates win the final factor.

nodes.name: Gallagher's 0-1 law
nodes.statement: Consider a function $\psi:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{R}_{\geqslant0}$ and let $\mathcal{A}$ be as in \eqref{eq:A-dfn}. Then either $\lambda(\mathcal{A})=0$ or $\lambda(\mathcal{A})=1$.
nodes.label: lem:Gallagher

nodes.name: Citation for Gallagher's 0-1 law
nodes.statement: This is Theorem 1 of \cite{gallagher}.

nodes.name: Duffin-Schaeffer conjecture when psi only takes large values
nodes.statement: Let $\psi:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}_{\geqslant 0}$ be a function, and let $\mathcal{A}$ be as in \eqref{eq:A-dfn}. Assume, further, that: \begin{enumerate} \item For every $q\in\mathbb{Z}$, either $\psi(q)=0$ or $\psi(q)\geqslant 1/2$; \item $\sum_{q=1}^\infty \psi(q)\varphi(q)/q=\infty$. \end{enumerate} Then $\lambda(\mathcal{A})=1$.
nodes.label: lem:Large

nodes.name: Citation for the large-values case
nodes.statement: This follows from \cite[Theorem 2]{PV}.

nodes.name: Pollington-Vaughan overlap bound
nodes.statement: Consider a function $\psi:\mathbb{N}\to[0,1/2]$ and let $\mathcal{A}_q$ be as in \eqref{eq:A_q-dfn}. In addition, given $q,r\in\mathbb{N}$, set \[ M(q,r):=\max\{r\psi(q),q\psi(r)\}. \] If $q\neq r$, then we have \[ \frac{\lambda(\mathcal{A}_q\cap \mathcal{A}_r)} {\lambda(\mathcal{A}_q)\lambda(\mathcal{A}_r)} \ll \mathds{1}_{M(q,r)\geqslant \gcd(q,r)} \prod_{\substack{p|qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p>M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)}} \left(1+\frac{1}{p}\right) . \]
nodes.statement_short: $\lambda(\mathcal{A}_q\cap\mathcal{A}_r)/\lambda(\mathcal{A}_q)\lambda(\mathcal{A}_r)$ is bounded by a product over primes dividing exactly one of $q,r$.
nodes.label: lem:Pollington

nodes.name: Citation for the overlap bound
nodes.statement: This bound is given in \cite[p. 195-196]{PV}.

nodes.name: L_t(a,b)
nodes.statement: Given the above lemma, we introduce the notation \begin{equation} L_t(a,b):= \sum_{\substack{p|ab/\gcd(a,b)^2 \\ p\geqslant t}} \frac{1}{p} \end{equation} for $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$ and $t\geqslant1$.
nodes.statement_short: $L_t(a,b)$ is the sum of $1/p$ over primes $p\ge t$ dividing $ab/\gcd(a,b)^2$.

nodes.name: Definition of L_t
nodes.statement: L_t(a,b):= \sum_{\substack{p|ab/\gcd(a,b)^2 \\ p\geqslant t}} \frac{1}{p}
nodes.label: eq:L_t-dfn

nodes.name: Second moment bound
nodes.statement: Let $\psi$ and $M(q,r)$ be as in as in Lemma \ref{lem:Pollington}, and consider $Y\geqslant X\geqslant1$ such that \[ 1\leqslant \sum_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y} \frac{\psi(q)\varphi(q)}{q} \leqslant2 . \] For each $t\geqslant1$, set \eq{ \mathcal{E}_t = \big\{(v,w)\in (\mathbb{Z}\cap[X,Y])^2 : \gcd(v,w)\geqslant t^{-1}\cdot M(v,w) ,\ L_t(v,w) \geqslant 10 \big\}. } Then \[ \sum_{(v,w)\in \mathcal{E}_t} \frac{\varphi(v)\psi(v)}{v}\cdot \frac{\varphi(w)\psi(w)}{w} \ll \frac{1}{t} . \]
nodes.statement_short: Weighted measure of pairs with gcd $\ge M(v,w)/t$ and $L_t(v,w)\ge10$ is $O(1/t)$.
nodes.label: prop:GCD

nodes.name: Edge set E_t
nodes.statement: \mathcal{E}_t = \big\{(v,w)\in (\mathbb{Z}\cap[X,Y])^2 : \gcd(v,w)\geqslant t^{-1}\cdot M(v,w) ,\ L_t(v,w) \geqslant 10 \big\}.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1 assuming Proposition 5.4
nodes.statement: We wish to prove that \begin{equation} \lambda(\mathcal{A})=1, \end{equation} where $\mathcal{A}=\limsup_{q\to\infty}\mathcal{A}_q$ with $\mathcal{A}_q$ defined by \eqref{eq:A-dfn}. We first write \[ \psi(q)=\psi_1(q)+\psi_2(q), \qquad\text{where}\qquad \psi_1(q) =\begin{cases} \psi(q)&\text{if}\ \psi(q)>1/2,\\ 0&\text{otherwise} . \end{cases} \] In particular, $\psi_2(q)=\psi(q)$ if $\psi(q)\leqslant 1/2$, and $\psi_2(q)=0$ otherwise. If it so happens that $\sum_{q=1}^\infty \psi_1(q)\varphi(q)/q=\infty$, then we apply Lemma \ref{lem:Large} to $\psi_1$ to find that $\lambda(\limsup_{q\to\infty}\mathcal{B}_q)=1$, where $\mathcal{B}_q$ is defined as $\mathcal{A}_q$ but with $\psi$ replaced by $\psi_1$. This proves \eqref{eq:MainGoal}, since $\psi_1(q)\leqslant \psi(q)$, and so $\mathcal{B}_q\subseteq\mathcal{A}_q$. Therefore we may assume without loss of generality that $\sum_{q=1}^\infty \psi_1(q)\varphi(q)/q<\infty$, and so $\sum_{q=1}^\infty \psi_2(q)\varphi(q)/q=\infty$. Thus, we have reduced Theorem \ref{thm:MainThm} to the case when \[ \psi(q)\leqslant 1/2\quad\text{for all}\ q\geqslant1. \] By Lemma \ref{lem:Gallagher}, the Duffin-Schaeffer conjecture will follow if we prove that $\lambda(\mathcal{A})>0$, since this means $\mathcal{A}$ cannot have measure 0. Note that \begin{equation} \mathcal{A}=\limsup_{q\to\infty}\mathcal{A}_q = \bigcap_{j=1}^{\infty} \bigcup_{q\geqslant j}\mathcal{A}_q . \end{equation} Now, let $X$ be a large parameter and fix $Y=Y(X)$ to be minimal such that \[ \sum_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y} \frac{\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q} \in[1,2] . \] (Such a $Y$ exists since $\psi(q)\leqslant 1/2$ for all $q$.) Hence, we see that it suffices to prove that \begin{equation} \lambda\bigg(\bigcup_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y} \mathcal{A}_q\bigg)\gg1 \end{equation} uniformly for all large enough $X$, since this implies that $\lambda(\mathcal{A})>0$ by virtue of \eqref{eq:limsup-rewrite}, and hence Theorem \ref{thm:MainThm} follows. For each $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$, consider the counting function \[ Q(\alpha)=\#\{q\in\mathbb{Z}\cap [X,Y]: \alpha\in\mathcal{A}_q\} = \sum_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y} \mathds{1}_{\mathcal{A}_q}(\alpha). \] We then have \begin{align*} \mathrm{supp}(Q)&=\bigcup_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y}\mathcal{A}_q,\\ \int_0^1 Q(\alpha) \mathrm{d}\alpha &= \sum_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y}\lambda(\mathcal{A}_q) \geqslant \sum_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y} \frac{\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q} \geqslant 1 ,\\ \int_0^1 Q(\alpha)^2 \mathrm{d}\alpha &= \sum_{X\leqslant q,r \leqslant Y}\lambda(\mathcal{A}_q\cap \mathcal{A}_r) . \end{align*} Hence, the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality implies that \[ \lambda\bigg(\bigcup_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y}\mathcal{A}_q\bigg)\int_0^1 Q(\alpha)^2\mathrm{d}\alpha \geqslant\Bigl(\int_0^1Q(\alpha)\mathrm{d} \alpha\Bigr)^2\geqslant1. \] Thus, to establish \eqref{eq:Finite}, it is enough to prove that \begin{equation} \sum_{X\leqslant q,r\leqslant Y} \lambda(\mathcal{A}_q\cap \mathcal{A}_r) \ll 1 . \end{equation} The terms with $q=r$ contribute a total \[ \sum_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y}\lambda(\mathcal{A}_q)\leqslant \sum_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y} \frac{2\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q}\leqslant 4, \] and so we only need to consider the contribution of those terms with $q\ne r$. Applying Lemma \ref{lem:Pollington}, we see that \[ \lambda(\mathcal{A}_q\cap \mathcal{A}_r)\ll \mathds{1}_{M(q,r)\geqslant \gcd(q,r)}\cdot \frac{\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q}\cdot \frac{\varphi(r)\psi(r)}{r}\cdot \prod_{\substack{p|qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p>M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)}} \left(1+\frac{1}{p}\right) , \] where we recall that \[ M(q,r)=\max\{r\psi(q),q\psi(r)\}. \] Thus, \eqref{eq:2ndmoment-goal} is reduced to showing that \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{X\leqslant q,r\leqslant Y \\ M(q,r)\geqslant\gcd(q,r) }} \frac{\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q} \cdot\frac{\varphi(r)\psi(r)}{r} \prod_{\substack{p|qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p>M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)}}\left(1+\frac{1}{p}\right) \ll 1. \end{equation} To prove this inequality, we divide the range of $q$ and $r$ into convenient subsets. The pairs $(q,r)\in (\mathbb{Z}\cap [X,Y])^2$ with \[ \prod_{\substack{p|qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p>M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)}}\left(1+\frac{1}{p}\right) < e^{100} \] contribute a total of at most \[ e^{100}\bigg(\sum_{q\in [X,Y] } \frac{\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q}\bigg)^2 \leqslant 4e^{100} \] to the right hand side of \eqref{eq:goal}, and so can be ignored. For any other pair $(q,r)$, we see that \[ e^{100} \leqslant \prod_{\substack{p|qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p>M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)}}\left(1+\frac{1}{p}\right) \leqslant \exp\Bigl(\sum_{\substack{p|qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p>M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)}}\frac{1}{p}\Bigr), \] so certainly we have \[ \sum_{p|qr/\gcd(q,r)^2}\frac{1}{p} \geqslant 100. \] For any such pair, we let $j=j(q,r)$ be the largest integer such that \[ \sum_{\substack{p| qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p\geqslant \exp\exp(j)}} \frac{1}{p} \geqslant 10. \] Since $j$ is chosen maximally, we have \[ \sum_{\substack{p| qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p\geqslant \exp\exp(j+1)}} \frac{1}{p} <10 . \] Mertens' theorem then implies that \[ \sum_{\substack{p| qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p\geqslant \exp\exp(j)}} \frac{1}{p}=\sum_{\substack{p| qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ \exp\exp(j)\leqslant p <\exp\exp(j+1)}} \frac{1}{p}+\sum_{\substack{p| qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p\geqslant \exp\exp(j+1)}} \frac{1}{p} \ll 1 . \] Therefore \als{ \prod_{\substack{p| qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p>M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)}}\left(1+\frac{1}{p}\right) &\ll \prod_{M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)<p\leqslant \exp\exp(j)} \left(1+\frac{1}{p}\right) \\ &\ll\begin{cases} 1&\text{if}\ M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)\geqslant \exp\exp(j),\\ e^j &\text{otherwise}, \end{cases} } where we used again Mertens' theorem. As above, those pairs with \[ \prod_{\substack{p| qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p>M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)}}\left(1+\frac{1}{p}\right)\ll 1 \] make an acceptable contribution to \eqref{eq:goal}. Therefore we only need to consider pairs $(q,r)$ with $M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)< \exp\exp(j)$. We have thus reduced \eqref{eq:goal} to showing that \begin{equation} \sum_{j\geqslant 0} e^j \sum_{(q,r)\in \mathcal{E}_{\exp\exp(j)}} \frac{\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q}\cdot \frac{\varphi(r)\psi(r)}{r} \ll 1, \end{equation} where $\mathcal{E}_t$ is defined by \eqref{eq:E_t}. To prove \eqref{eq:goal2}, we apply Proposition \ref{prop:GCD}, which shows that the inner sum is $O(1/\exp\exp(j))$. Since the sum of $e^j/\exp\exp(j)$ over $j\geqslant 0$ converges, this completes the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:MainThm}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to $\psi\le1/2$, use Gallagher's 0-1 law and a Cauchy-Schwarz second moment bound. The overlap sum is split dyadically in $j$ via Mertens' theorem and bounded by Proposition 5.4.

nodes.name: Main goal
nodes.statement: \lambda(\mathcal{A})=1,
nodes.label: eq:MainGoal

nodes.name: limsup rewrite
nodes.statement: \mathcal{A}=\limsup_{q\to\infty}\mathcal{A}_q = \bigcap_{j=1}^{\infty} \bigcup_{q\geqslant j}\mathcal{A}_q .
nodes.label: eq:limsup-rewrite

nodes.name: Finite union lower bound
nodes.statement: \lambda\bigg(\bigcup_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y} \mathcal{A}_q\bigg)\gg1
nodes.label: eq:Finite

nodes.name: Second moment goal
nodes.statement: \sum_{X\leqslant q,r\leqslant Y} \lambda(\mathcal{A}_q\cap \mathcal{A}_r) \ll 1 .
nodes.label: eq:2ndmoment-goal

nodes.name: Overlap sum goal
nodes.statement: \sum_{\substack{X\leqslant q,r\leqslant Y \\ M(q,r)\geqslant\gcd(q,r) }} \frac{\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q} \cdot\frac{\varphi(r)\psi(r)}{r} \prod_{\substack{p|qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p>M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)}}\left(1+\frac{1}{p}\right) \ll 1.
nodes.label: eq:goal

nodes.name: Dyadic overlap goal
nodes.statement: \sum_{j\geqslant 0} e^j \sum_{(q,r)\in \mathcal{E}_{\exp\exp(j)}} \frac{\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q}\cdot \frac{\varphi(r)\psi(r)}{r} \ll 1,
nodes.label: eq:goal2

nodes.name: GCD graph
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a septuple $(\mu,\mathcal{V},\mathcal{W},\mathcal{E},\mathcal{P},f,g)$ such that: \begin{enumerate} \item $\mu$ is a measure on $\mathbb{N}$ such that $\mu(n)<\infty$ for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$; we extend to $\mathbb{N}^2$ by letting \[ \mu(\mathcal{N}):=\sum_{(n_1,n_2)\in\mathcal{N}}\mu(n_1)\mu(n_2) \quad\text{for}\quad\mathcal{N}\subseteq\mathbb{N}^2; \] \item $\mathcal{V}$ and $\mathcal{W}$ are finite sets of positive integers; \item $\mathcal{E}\subseteq\mathcal{V}\times \mathcal{W}$, that is to say $(\mathcal{V},\mathcal{W},\mathcal{E})$ is a bipartite graph; \item $\mathcal{P}$ is a set of primes; \item $f$ and $g$ are functions from $\mathcal{P}$ to $\mathbb{Z}_{\geqslant0}$ such that for all $p\in\mathcal{P}$ we have: \begin{enumerate} \item $p^{f(p)}|v$ for all $v\in\mathcal{V}$, and $p^{g(p)}|w$ for all $w\in\mathcal{W}$; \item if $(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}$, then $p^{\min\{f(p),g(p)\}}\|\gcd(v,w)$; \item if $f(p)\neq g(p)$, then $p^{f(p)}\|v$ for all $v\in\mathcal{V}$, and $p^{g(p)}\|w$ for all $w\in\mathcal{W}$. \end{enumerate} \end{enumerate} We then call $G$ a (bipartite) \emph{GCD graph} with \emph{sets of vertices} $(\mathcal{V},\mathcal{W})$, \emph{set of edges} $\mathcal{E}$ and \emph{multiplicative data} $(\mathcal{P},f,g)$. We will also refer to $\mathcal{P}$ as the \emph{set of primes} of $G$. If $\mathcal{P}=\emptyset$, we say that $G$ has \emph{trivial} set of primes and we view $f=f_\emptyset$ and $g=g_\emptyset$ as two copies of the empty function from $\emptyset$ to $\mathbb{Z}_{\geqslant 0}$.
nodes.statement_short: A weighted bipartite graph on integers with prime set $\mathcal{P}$ and exponents $f,g$ fixing the $p$-adic valuations of vertices and gcds.
nodes.label: gcd graph dfn

nodes.name: Non-trivial GCD graph
nodes.statement: Let $G=(\mu,\mathcal{V},\mathcal{W},\mathcal{E},\mathcal{P},f,g)$. We say that $G$ is {\it non-trivial} if $\mu(\mathcal{E})>0$.
nodes.label: non-trivial gcd graph dfn

nodes.name: Edge set bound
nodes.statement: Let $\psi:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}_{\geqslant 0}$, $t\geqslant1$ and $\mu$ be the measure $\mu(v)=\psi(v)\varphi(v)/v$. Let $\mathcal{V}\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $0<\mu(\mathcal{V})\ll 1$. Let $G=(\mu,\mathcal{V},\mathcal{V},\mathcal{E},\emptyset,f_\emptyset,g_\emptyset)$ be a bipartite GCD graph with measure $\mu$, vertex sets $\mathcal{V}$, trivial set of primes, and edge set $\mathcal{E}\subseteq\mathcal{E}_t$, where $\mathcal{E}_t$ is defined as in Proposition \ref{prop:GCD}. Then \[ \mu(\mathcal{E})\ll 1/t. \]
nodes.statement_short: For the GCD graph on $\mathcal{V}$ with edges in $\mathcal{E}_t$ and weights $\psi(v)\varphi(v)/v$, $\mu(\mathcal{E})\ll1/t$.
nodes.label: prop:Graph

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.4 assuming Proposition 6.3
nodes.statement: Recall the notation $\psi$, $M(q,r)$, $L_t(a,b)$, $X$, $Y$ and $\mathcal{E}_t$ of Proposition \ref{prop:GCD}. We wish to show that \begin{equation} \sum_{(v_1,v_2)\in \mathcal{E}_t} \frac{\varphi(v_1)\psi(v_1)}{v_1}\cdot \frac{\varphi(v_2)\psi(v_2)}{v_2} \ll \frac{1}{t} . \end{equation} Let $\mu$ be the measure on $\mathbb{N}$ defined by $\mu(v):=\psi(v)\varphi(v)/v$ and let $\mathcal{V}=\mathbb{Z}\cap[X,Y]$, so that \[ \mu(\mathcal{V})=\sum_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y}\frac{\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q}\in[1,2]. \] Now define $\mathcal{E}=\mathcal{E}_t$ to be as in Proposition \ref{prop:GCD}. We see that $(\mathcal{V},\mathcal{V},\mathcal{E})$ forms a bipartite graph with vertex sets two copies of $\mathcal{V}$ and edge set $\mathcal{E}$. We now turn this bipartite graph into a GCD graph $G=(\mu,\mathcal{V},\mathcal{V},\mathcal{E},\emptyset,f_\emptyset,g_\emptyset)$ by attaching trivial multiplicative data to the bipartite graph (here $f_\emptyset$ and $g_\emptyset$ are viewed as two copies of the function of the empty set to $\mathbb{Z}_{\geqslant 0}$). Since $0<\mu(\mathcal{V})\ll 1$, Proposition \ref{prop:Graph} now applies, showing that \[ \mu(\mathcal{E}_t)\ll 1/t. \] This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Recast the pair set $\mathcal{E}_t$ as a GCD graph with trivial primes and apply Proposition 6.3.

nodes.name: Target bound
nodes.statement: \sum_{(v_1,v_2)\in \mathcal{E}_t} \frac{\varphi(v_1)\psi(v_1)}{v_1}\cdot \frac{\varphi(v_2)\psi(v_2)}{v_2} \ll \frac{1}{t} .
nodes.label: eq:Target

nodes.name: GCD subgraph
nodes.statement: Let $G=(\mu,\mathcal{V},\mathcal{W},\mathcal{E},\mathcal{P},f,g)$ and $G'=(\mu',\mathcal{V}',\mathcal{W}',\mathcal{E}',\mathcal{P}',f',g')$ be two GCD graphs. We say that $G'$ is a \emph{GCD subgraph} of $G$ if: \[ \mu'=\mu,\quad \mathcal{V}'\subseteq\mathcal{V},\quad \mathcal{W}'\subseteq\mathcal{W},\quad \mathcal{E}'\subseteq\mathcal{E}, \quad \mathcal{P}'\supseteq\mathcal{P}, \quad f'\big|_{\mathcal{P}}=f,\quad g'\big|_{\mathcal{P}}=g. \] We write $G'\preceq G$ if $G'$ is a GCD subgraph of $G$. Lastly, we say that $G'$ is a {\it non-trivial GCD subgraph} of $G$ if $\mu(\mathcal{E}')>0$, that is to say $G'$ is non-trivial as a GCD graph.
nodes.statement_short: $G'\preceq G$: same measure, smaller vertex and edge sets, larger prime set, and $f',g'$ extend $f,g$.

nodes.name: Special GCD subgraphs from prime power divisibility
nodes.statement: Let $p$ be a prime number, and let $k,\ell\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geqslant0}$. \begin{enumerate} \item If $\mathcal{V}$ is a set of integers and $k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geqslant0}$, we set \[ \mathcal{V}_{p^k}=\{v\in\mathcal{V}:p^k\|v\}, \] that is to say $\mathcal{V}_{p^k}$ is the set of integers in $\mathcal{V}$ whose $p$-adic valuation is exactly $k$. Here we have the understanding that $\mathcal{V}_{p^0}$ denotes the set of $v\in\mathcal{V}$ that are coprime to $p$. In particular, $\mathcal{V}_{2^0}$ and $\mathcal{V}_{3^0}$ denote different sets of integers. \item Let $G=(\mathcal{V},\mathcal{W},\mathcal{E})$ be a bipartite graph. If $\mathcal{V}'\subseteq\mathcal{V}$ and $\mathcal{W}'\subseteq\mathcal{W}$, we define \[ \mathcal{E}(\mathcal{V}',\mathcal{W}'):=\mathcal{E}\cap(\mathcal{V}'\times\mathcal{W}'). \] We also write for brevity \[ \mathcal{E}_{p^k,p^\ell}:=\mathcal{E}(\mathcal{V}_{p^k},\mathcal{W}_{p^\ell}) . \] \item Let $G=(\mu,\mathcal{V},\mathcal{W},\mathcal{E},\mathcal{P},f,g)$ be a GCD graph such that $p\notin \mathcal{P}$. We then define the septuple \[ G_{p^k,p^\ell}=(\mu,\mathcal{V}_{p^k},\mathcal{W}_{p^\ell},\mathcal{E}_{p^k,p^\ell},\mathcal{P}\cup\{p\},f_{p^k},g_{p^\ell}) \] where the functions $f_{p^k}$, $g_{p^\ell}$ are defined on $\mathcal{P}\cup\{p\}$ by the relations $f_{p^k}\vert_{\mathcal{P}}=f$, $g_{p^\ell}\vert_{\mathcal{P}}=g$, \[ f_{p^k}(p)=k\quad\text{and}\quad g_{p^\ell}(p)=\ell. \] It is easy to check that $G_{p^k,p^\ell}$ is a GCD subgraph of $G$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Restrict vertices to exact $p$-adic valuations $k,\ell$ and add $p$ to the prime set with $f(p)=k$, $g(p)=\ell$.
nodes.label: def:special graphs

nodes.name: Quantities associated to GCD graphs
nodes.statement: Let $G=(\mu,\mathcal{V},\mathcal{W},\mathcal{E},\mathcal{P},f,g)$ be a GCD graph. \begin{enumerate} \item If $\mu(\mathcal{V}),\mu(\mathcal{W})>0$, then we define the \emph{edge density} of $G$ by \[ \delta=\delta(G):=\frac{\mu(\mathcal{E})}{\mu(\mathcal{V})\mu(\mathcal{W})}. \] If $\mu(\mathcal{V})=0$ or $\mu(\mathcal{W})=0$, we define the edge density of $G$ to be $0$. \item The \emph{neighbourhood sets} are defined by \[ \Gamma_G(v):=\{w\in\mathcal{W}:\,(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}\}\quad\text{for any}\ v\in\mathcal{V}, \] and similarly \[ \Gamma_G(w):=\{v\in\mathcal{V}:\,(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}\} \quad\text{for any}\ w\in \mathcal{W}. \] \item We let $\mathcal{R}(G)$ be given by \[ \mathcal{R}(G):= \{p\notin\mathcal{P}: \exists (v,w)\in\mathcal{E}\ \text{such that}\ p|\gcd(v,w)\} . \] That is to say $\mathcal{R}(G)$ is the set of primes occurring in a GCD which we haven't yet accounted for. We split this into two further subsets: \[ \mathcal{R}^\sharp(G):=\left\{p\in\mathcal{R}(G): \exists k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geqslant0}\ \text{such that}\ \frac{\mu(\mathcal{V}_{p^k})}{\mu(\mathcal{V})},\frac{\mu(\mathcal{W}_{p^k})}{\mu(\mathcal{W})}\geqslant 1-\frac{10^{40}}{p}\right\} \] and \[ \mathcal{R}^\flat(G):=\mathcal{R}(G)\setminus \mathcal{R}^\sharp(G). \] \item The \emph{quality} of $G$ is defined by \als{ q(G)&:= \delta^{10}\mu(\mathcal{V})\mu(\mathcal{W}) \prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}} \frac{p^{|f(p)-g(p)|}}{(1-\mathds{1}_{f(p)=g(p)\geqslant1}/p)^2(1-1/p^{31/30})^{10}}, } where $\delta$ is the edge density of $G$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Edge density, neighbourhoods, unaccounted gcd primes $\mathcal{R}=\mathcal{R}^\sharp\sqcup\mathcal{R}^\flat$, and the quality $q(G)$.

nodes.name: Alternative formula for the quality
nodes.statement: If $\mu(\mathcal{V}),\mu(\mathcal{W})>0$ we see that \als{ q(G)&= \frac{\mu(\mathcal{E})^{10}}{\mu(\mathcal{V})^{9}\mu(\mathcal{W})^{9}} \prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}} \frac{p^{|f(p)-g(p)|}}{(1-\mathds{1}_{f(p)=g(p)\geqslant1}/p)^2(1-1/p^{31/30})^{10}} . }

nodes.name: Role of the factors in the quality
nodes.statement: As mentioned in Section \ref{sec:outline}, there are two natural candidates for a quantity to increment; either $\delta$ or $\mu(\mathcal{V})\mu(\mathcal{W})\prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}}p^{|f(p)-g(p)|}$ (this is the natural generalization to non-squarefree integers). One should essentially think of the quality as a `hybrid' of the two quantities, but with some additional factors which are included for technical reasons. The factor \[ \prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}}\frac{1}{(1-1/p^{31/30})^{10}} \] always lies in the interval $[1,\zeta(31/30)^{10}]$, and so is always of size bounded away from 0 and from $\infty$. This factor is included merely for convenience, and allows us to have a quality increment even if there is a tiny loss in our arguments in terms of $p$. The factor \[ \prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}}\frac{1}{(1-\mathds{1}_{f(p)=g(p)\geqslant 1}/p)^2} \] is crucial for the proof of a quality increment in Lemma \ref{lem:MainLem2} and Proposition \ref{prop:IterationStep2}. This is related to the technical point that it is vital that the weights of our vertices contain the factor $\varphi(q)/q$. We will discuss this feature in more detail in Section \ref{sec:Concluding}.
nodes.statement_short: Quality is a hybrid of density and size; the $\zeta(31/30)$-bounded factor absorbs tiny losses and the $(1-1/p)^{-2}$ factor reflects the $\varphi(q)/q$ weights.

nodes.name: Basic properties of GCD graphs
nodes.statement: Let $G_1,G_2,G_3$ be GCD graphs. \begin{enumerate} \item The property of being a GCD subgraph is transitive: If $G_1\preceq G_2$ and $G_2\preceq G_3$, then $G_1\preceq G_3$ \item If $G_1\preceq G_2$, then $\mathcal{R}(G_1)\subseteq \mathcal{R}(G_2)$. \item If $G_1=(\mu,\mathcal{V},\mathcal{W},\mathcal{E},\mathcal{P},f,g)$ is non-trivial, then $\mu(\mathcal{V}),\mu(\mathcal{W})>0$. \item Let $G_1$ have edge density $\delta$. Then the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $G_1$ is non-trivial. \item $\delta>0$. \item $q(G_1)>0$. \end{enumerate} \end{enumerate}
conclusions: The property of being a GCD subgraph is transitive: If $G_1\preceq G_2$ and $G_2\preceq G_3$, then $G_1\preceq G_3$ \item If $G_1\preceq G_2$, then $\mathcal{R}(G_1)\subseteq \mathcal{R}(G_2)$. \item If $G_1=(\mu,\mathcal{V},\mathcal{W},\mathcal{E},\mathcal{P},f,g)$ is non-trivial, then $\mu(\mathcal{V}),\mu(\mathcal{W})>0$. \item Let $G_1$ have edge density $\delta$. Then the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $G_1$ is non-trivial. \item $\delta>0$. \item $q(G_1)>0$.
nodes.label: lem:Trivial

nodes.name: Proof of basic properties
nodes.statement: All statements are immediate from the definition of GCD subgraphs and of non-trivial GCD graphs.

nodes.name: R-flat and R-sharp are not monotone
nodes.statement: In part (b) of Lemma \ref{lem:Trivial}, it is not necessarily the case that $\mathcal{R}^\flat(G_1)\subseteq\mathcal{R}^\flat(G_2)$ nor that $\mathcal{R}^\sharp(G_1)\subseteq \mathcal{R}^\sharp(G_2)$.

nodes.name: Existence of a good GCD subgraph
nodes.statement: Let $G=(\mu,\mathcal{V},\mathcal{W},\mathcal{E},\emptyset,f_\emptyset,g_\emptyset)$ be a GCD graph with trivial set of primes and edge density $\delta>0$. Assume further that \[ \mathcal{E}\subseteq\{(v,w)\in\mathbb{N}^2 : L_t(v,w) \geqslant10\} \] for some $t$ satisfying \[ t\geqslant10\delta^{-1/50}\quad\text{and}\quad t> 10^{2000}. \] Then there is a GCD subgraph $G'=(\mu,\mathcal{V}',\mathcal{W}',\mathcal{E}',\mathcal{P}',f',g')$ of $G$ with edge density $\delta'>0$ such that: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)] \item $\mathcal{R}(G')=\emptyset$; \item For all $v\in\mathcal{V}'$, we have $\mu(\Gamma_{G'}(v))\geqslant(9\delta'/10)\mu(\mathcal{W}')$; \item For all $w\in\mathcal{W}'$, we have $\mu(\Gamma_{G'}(w))\geqslant(9\delta'/10)\mu(\mathcal{V}')$; \item One of the following holds: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item $q(G')\gg \delta t^{50} q(G)$; \item $q(G')\gg q(G)$, and if $(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}'$ and we write them as $v=v'\prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}'}p^{f'(p)}$ and $w=w'\prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}'}p^{g'(p)}$, then $L_t(v',w')\geqslant 4$. \end{enumerate} \end{enumerate}
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph
nodes.statement_short: A GCD graph with $L_t\ge10$ edges has a subgraph with no unaccounted gcd primes, high degrees, and a large quality gain or anatomical condition $L_t(v',w')\ge4$.
conclusions: Then there is a GCD subgraph $G'=(\mu,\mathcal{V}',\mathcal{W}',\mathcal{E}',\mathcal{P}',f',g')$ of $G$ with edge density $\delta'>0$ such that: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)] \item $\mathcal{R}(G')=\emptyset$; \item For all $v\in\mathcal{V}'$, we have $\mu(\Gamma_{G'}(v))\geqslant(9\delta'/10)\mu(\mathcal{W}')$; \item For all $w\in\mathcal{W}'$, we have $\mu(\Gamma_{G'}(w))\geqslant(9\delta'/10)\mu(\mathcal{V}')$; \item One of the following holds: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item $q(G')\gg \delta t^{50} q(G)$; \item $q(G')\gg q(G)$, and if $(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}'$ and we write them as $v=v'\prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}'}p^{f'(p)}$ and $w=w'\prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}'}p^{g'(p)}$, then $L_t(v',w')\geqslant 4$.
nodes.label: prop:BoundOnEdges

nodes.name: Bounds on multiplicative functions
nodes.statement: Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and write $\tau_k$ for the $k$-th divisor function. If $f$ is a multiplicative function such that $0\leqslant f\leqslant \tau_k$, then \[ \sum_{n\leqslant x} f(n) \ll_k x \cdot \exp\Big\{\sum_{p\leqslant x}\frac{f(p)-1}{p}\Big\} . \]
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph
assumptions: $f$ is a multiplicative function such that $0\leqslant f\leqslant \tau_k$
nodes.label: lem:Tenenbaum

nodes.name: Citation for multiplicative function bound
nodes.statement: This is \cite[Theorem 14.2, p. 145]{dk-book}.
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph

nodes.name: Few numbers with many prime factors
nodes.statement: For $x,t\geqslant1$ and $c\in[1,10]$, we have \[ \#\bigg\{n\leqslant x: \sum_{\substack{p|n\\ p\geqslant t}}\frac{1}{p} \geqslant c \bigg\} \ll x\exp\{ - t^{e^{c-1}}\} \, ; \] the implied constant is absolute.
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph
nodes.statement_short: Integers $n\le x$ with $\sum_{p|n,p\ge t}1/p\ge c$ number $\ll x\exp(-t^{e^{c-1}})$.
conclusions: \#\bigg\{n\leqslant x: \sum_{\substack{p|n\\ p\geqslant t}}\frac{1}{p} \geqslant c \bigg\} \ll x\exp\{ - t^{e^{c-1}}\}
nodes.label: lem:Anatomy

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7.3
nodes.statement:
We may assume that $t$ is large enough, since the result is trivial when $t$ is bounded. Set $T=t^{e^{c-1}}$, so that $\sum_{t\leqslant p<T}1/p \leqslant c-1/2$ by Mertens' theorem. Hence  egin{equation} \# igg\{n\leqslant x:\sum_{\substack{p|n\ p\geqslant t}} rac{1}{p} \geqslant c  igg\} \leqslant \# igg\{n\leqslant x: \sum_{\substack{p|n\ p\geqslant T}} rac{1}{p} \geqslant 1/2  igg\} \leqslant e^{-T} \sum_{n\leqslant x} \prod_{\substack{p|n\ p\geqslant T}} e^{2T/p} . \end{equation} We wish to apply Lemma ef{lem:Tenenbaum} when $f$ is the multiplicative function with $f(p^
u)=e^{2T/p}$ for $p\geqslant T$ and all $

u)\leqslant e^2\leqslant 8$ for all prime powers $p^
u$, so that $f\leqslant 	au_8$. Thus \[ \sum_{n\leqslant x} \prod_{p|n,\ p\geqslant T} e^{2T/p} = \sum_{n\leqslant x} f(n) \ll x \cdot \exp\Big\{\sum_{p\leqslant x}  rac{f(p)-1}{p}\Big\} = x \cdot \exp\Big\{\sum_{T\leqslant p\leqslant x}  rac{e^{2T/p}-1}{p}\Big\} . \] Since $e^{2T/p}=1+O(T/p)$ for $p\geqslant T$, and $\sum_{p\geqslant T} T/p^2\ll1$, the sum of $(e^{2T/p}-1)/p$ over $p\in[T,x]$ is $O(1)$. We thus conclude that \[ \#\Big\{n\leqslant x:\sum_{\substack{p|n\ p\geqslant t}} rac{1}{p} \geqslant c \Big\}\ll e^{-T}x. \] Since $T=t^{e^{c-1}}$, the lemma has been proven.
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph
nodes.statement_short: Rankin's trick with $T=t^{e^{c-1}}$ and Mertens, then Lemma 7.2 bounds the resulting multiplicative sum.

nodes.name: Rankin trick bound
nodes.statement: \#\bigg\{n\leqslant x:\sum_{\substack{p|n\\ p\geqslant t}}\frac{1}{p} \geqslant c \bigg\} \leqslant \#\bigg\{n\leqslant x: \sum_{\substack{p|n\\ p\geqslant T}}\frac{1}{p} \geqslant 1/2 \bigg\} \leqslant e^{-T} \sum_{n\leqslant x} \prod_{\substack{p|n\\ p\geqslant T}} e^{2T/p} .
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph
nodes.label: eq:Rankin

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.3 assuming Proposition 7.1
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph
nodes.statement_short: Apply Proposition 7.1 and bound $q(G')$ by counting multiples of $a,b$ below the largest neighbours. In case (ii) Lemma 7.3 gives an extra $e^{-t}$.

nodes.name: Quality upper bound for G'
nodes.statement: q(G') &= (\delta')^{10}\mu(\mathcal{V}')\mu(\mathcal{W}') \prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}'} \frac{p^{|f'(p)-g'(p)|}}{(1-\mathds{1}_{f'(p)=g'(p)\geqslant1}/p)^2(1-1/p^{31/30})^{10}}\nonumber\\ & \ll (\delta')^{10} \mu(\mathcal{V}')\mu(\mathcal{W}') \frac{ab}{\gcd(a,b)^2} \cdot \frac{ab}{\varphi(a)\varphi(b)}\nonumber \\ &= (\delta')^{9}\mu(\mathcal{E}') \frac{ab}{\gcd(a,b)^2} \cdot \frac{ab}{\varphi(a)\varphi(b)} .
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph
nodes.label: eq:QG'Bound

nodes.name: Upper bound for psi
nodes.statement: \psi(v)\leqslant \frac{t\cdot \gcd(a,b)}{w_{\max}(v)} \quad\text{and}\quad \psi(w)\leqslant \frac{t\cdot \gcd(a,b)}{v_{\max}(w)} \quad\text{for all}\quad v\in \mathcal{V}',\,w\in\mathcal{W}'.
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph
nodes.label: psi ub

nodes.name: Largest neighbour
nodes.statement: w_{\max}(v)=w_0 \quad\text{for all}\quad(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}'' .
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph
nodes.label: eq:w0

nodes.name: Quality bound via E''
nodes.statement: q(G') \ll (\delta')^{8} \mu(\mathcal{E}'') \frac{a b}{\varphi(a)\varphi(b)}\cdot \frac{a b}{\gcd(a,b)^2} \leqslant \mu(\mathcal{E}'') \frac{ab}{\gcd(a,b)^2} \cdot \frac{ab}{\varphi(a)\varphi(b)} .
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph
nodes.label: eq:q(G') bound

nodes.name: Quality bound by reciprocal sum
nodes.statement: q(G') \ll t^2ab \sum_{(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}''} \frac{1}{v_{\max}(w) w_0} \leqslant t^2ab \sum_{(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}'} \frac{1}{v_{\max}(w) w_0} .
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph
nodes.label: eq:G'Quality

nodes.name: Anatomical lower bound in case 2
nodes.statement: L_t(v',w')\geqslant 4\quad\text{whenever}\quad(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}'.
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph
nodes.label: eq:L_t-lowerbound

nodes.name: Iteration when R-flat is non-empty
nodes.statement: Let $G=(\mu,\mathcal{V},\mathcal{W},\mathcal{E},\mathcal{P},f,g)$ be a GCD graph with edge density $\delta>0$ such that \[ \mathcal{R}(G)\subseteq\{p>10^{2000}\}\quad\text{and}\quad \mathcal{R}^\flat(G)\neq\emptyset. \] Then there is a GCD subgraph $G'$ of $G$ with edge density $\delta'>0$ and multiplicative data $(\mathcal{P}',f',g')$ such that \[ \mathcal{P}\subsetneq\mathcal{P}'\subseteq\mathcal{P}\cup\mathcal{R}(G), \quad \mathcal{R}(G')\subsetneq \mathcal{R}(G), \quad \min\bigg\{1,\frac{\delta'}{\delta}\bigg\} \cdot \frac{q(G')}{q(G)}\geqslant 2^N , \] where $N=\#\{p\in\mathcal{P}'\setminus \mathcal{P}:f'(p)\neq g'(p)\}$.
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions
nodes.statement_short: If some unaccounted large prime is not almost-uniform, pass to a subgraph gaining $2^N$ in quality times density.
conclusions: Then there is a GCD subgraph $G'$ of $G$ with edge density $\delta'>0$ and multiplicative data $(\mathcal{P}',f',g')$ such that \[ \mathcal{P}\subsetneq\mathcal{P}'\subseteq\mathcal{P}\cup\mathcal{R}(G), \quad \mathcal{R}(G')\subsetneq \mathcal{R}(G), \quad \min\bigg\{1,\frac{\delta'}{\delta}\bigg\} \cdot \frac{q(G')}{q(G)}\geqslant 2^N , \] where $N=\#\{p\in\mathcal{P}'\setminus \mathcal{P}:f'(p)\neq g'(p)\}$.
nodes.label: prop:IterationStep1

nodes.name: Iteration when R-flat is empty
nodes.statement: Let $G=(\mu,\mathcal{V},\mathcal{W},\mathcal{E},\mathcal{P},f,g)$ be a GCD graph with edge density $\delta>0$ such that \[ \mathcal{R}(G)\subseteq\{p> 10^{2000}\}, \quad \mathcal{R}^\flat(G)=\emptyset , \quad \mathcal{R}^\sharp(G)\neq\emptyset. \] Then there is a GCD subgraph $G'=(\mu,\mathcal{V}',\mathcal{W}',\mathcal{E}',\mathcal{P}',f',g')$ of $G$ such that \[ \mathcal{P}\subsetneq\mathcal{P}'\subseteq\mathcal{P}\cup\mathcal{R}(G), \quad \mathcal{R}(G')\subsetneq \mathcal{R}(G), \quad q(G')\geqslant q(G). \]
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions
nodes.statement_short: If all unaccounted primes are almost-uniform, pass to a subgraph with more primes and no quality loss.
conclusions: Then there is a GCD subgraph $G'=(\mu,\mathcal{V}',\mathcal{W}',\mathcal{E}',\mathcal{P}',f',g')$ of $G$ such that \[ \mathcal{P}\subsetneq\mathcal{P}'\subseteq\mathcal{P}\cup\mathcal{R}(G), \quad \mathcal{R}(G')\subsetneq \mathcal{R}(G), \quad q(G')\geqslant q(G).
nodes.label: prop:IterationStep2

nodes.name: Bounded quality loss for small primes
nodes.statement: Let $G=(\mu,\mathcal{V},\mathcal{W},\mathcal{E},\emptyset,f_\emptyset,g_\emptyset)$ be a GCD graph with edge density $\delta>0$ and trivial set of primes. Then there is a GCD subgraph $G'=(\mu,\mathcal{V}',\mathcal{W}',\mathcal{E}',\mathcal{P}',f',g')$ of $G$ with edge density $\delta'>0$ such that \[ \mathcal{P}'\subseteq\{p\leqslant 10^{2000}\}, \quad \mathcal{R}(G')\subseteq\{p> 10^{2000}\}, \quad \min\bigg\{1,\frac{\delta'}{\delta}\bigg\} \cdot \frac{q(G')}{q(G)}\geqslant \frac{1}{10^{10^{3000}}} . \]
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions
nodes.statement_short: All primes $\le10^{2000}$ can be absorbed into $\mathcal{P}$ at a bounded loss in quality and density.
conclusions: Then there is a GCD subgraph $G'=(\mu,\mathcal{V}',\mathcal{W}',\mathcal{E}',\mathcal{P}',f',g')$ of $G$ with edge density $\delta'>0$ such that \[ \mathcal{P}'\subseteq\{p\leqslant 10^{2000}\}, \quad \mathcal{R}(G')\subseteq\{p> 10^{2000}\}, \quad \min\bigg\{1,\frac{\delta'}{\delta}\bigg\} \cdot \frac{q(G')}{q(G)}\geqslant \frac{1}{10^{10^{3000}}} .
nodes.label: prop:SmallPrimes

nodes.name: Removing the effect of R(G) from L_t(v,w)
nodes.statement: Let $t\geqslant300$ and $G=(\mu,\mathcal{V},\mathcal{W},\mathcal{E},\mathcal{P},f,g)$ be a GCD graph with edge density $\delta>0$ such that \[ \mathcal{R}^\flat(G)=\emptyset, \quad \delta\geqslant (10/t)^{50}, \quad \mathcal{E}\subseteq\{(v,w)\in\mathcal{V}\times\mathcal{W}: L_t(v,w)\geqslant 10\}. \] Then there exists a GCD subgraph $G'=(\mu,\mathcal{V},\mathcal{W},\mathcal{E}',\mathcal{P},f,g)$ of $G$ such that \[ q(G')\geqslant \frac{q(G)}{2}>0\quad\text{and}\quad \mathcal{E}'\subseteq \bigg\{(v,w)\in\mathcal{V}\times\mathcal{W}: \sum_{\substack{p|v w/\gcd(v,w)^2\\p\geqslant t,\ p\notin \mathcal{R}(G)}}\frac{1}{p}\geqslant 5\bigg\}. \]
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions
nodes.statement_short: When $\mathcal{R}^\flat=\emptyset$, drop few edges so that primes outside $\mathcal{R}(G)$ still give prime sum $\ge5$.
conclusions: Then there exists a GCD subgraph $G'=(\mu,\mathcal{V},\mathcal{W},\mathcal{E}',\mathcal{P},f,g)$ of $G$ such that \[ q(G')\geqslant \frac{q(G)}{2}>0\quad\text{and}\quad \mathcal{E}'\subseteq \bigg\{(v,w)\in\mathcal{V}\times\mathcal{W}: \sum_{\substack{p|v w/\gcd(v,w)^2\\p\geqslant t,\ p\notin \mathcal{R}(G)}}\frac{1}{p}\geqslant 5\bigg\}.
nodes.label: lem:Cosmetic

nodes.name: Subgraph with high-degree vertices
nodes.statement: Let $G=(\mu,\mathcal{V},\mathcal{W},\mathcal{E},\mathcal{P},f,g)$ be a GCD graph with edge density $\delta>0$. Then there is a GCD subgraph $G'=(\mu,\mathcal{V}',\mathcal{W}',\mathcal{E}',\mathcal{P},f,g)$ of $G$ with edge density $\delta'>0$ such that: \begin{enumerate} \item $q(G')\geqslant q(G)$; \item $\delta'\geqslant \delta$; \item For all $v\in\mathcal{V}'$ and for all $w\in\mathcal{W}'$, we have \[ \mu(\Gamma_{G'}(v))\geqslant\frac{9\delta'}{10}\mu(\mathcal{W}') \quad\text{and}\quad \mu(\Gamma_{G'}(w))\geqslant\frac{9\delta'}{10}\mu(\mathcal{V}'). \] \end{enumerate}
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions
nodes.statement_short: Pass to a subgraph with no loss in quality or density in which every vertex has degree at least $9\delta'/10$ of the other side.
conclusions: Then there is a GCD subgraph $G'=(\mu,\mathcal{V}',\mathcal{W}',\mathcal{E}',\mathcal{P},f,g)$ of $G$ with edge density $\delta'>0$ such that: \begin{enumerate} \item $q(G')\geqslant q(G)$; \item $\delta'\geqslant \delta$; \item For all $v\in\mathcal{V}'$ and for all $w\in\mathcal{W}'$, we have \[ \mu(\Gamma_{G'}(v))\geqslant\frac{9\delta'}{10}\mu(\mathcal{W}') \quad\text{and}\quad \mu(\Gamma_{G'}(w))\geqslant\frac{9\delta'}{10}\mu(\mathcal{V}').
nodes.label: lem:HighDegreeSubgraph

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 7.1 assuming Propositions 8.1-8.3 and Lemmas 8.4-8.5
nodes.statement:
We will construct the required subgraph $G'$ in several stages. It suffices to produce a GCD subgraph $G'$ of $G$ satisfying only conclusions $(a)$ and $(d)$ of Proposition ef{prop:BoundOnEdges}, since an application of Lemma ef{lem:HighDegreeSubgraph} then produces a GCD subgraph satisfying all the conclusions. \medskip 
oindent 	extit{Stage 1: Obtaining a GCD subgraph $G^{(1)}$ with $\mathcal{R}(G^{(1)})\subseteq \{p> 10^{2000}\}$.} \medskip Since $G$ has set of primes equal to the empy set, we may apply Proposition ef{prop:SmallPrimes} to $G$ to produce a GCD subgraph $G^{(1)}=(\mu,\mathcal{V}^{(1)},\mathcal{W}^{(1)},\mathcal{E}^{(1)},\mathcal{P}^{(1)},f^{(1)},g^{(1)})$ of $G$ with edge density $\delta^{(1)}$ and for which  egin{equation} \mathcal{R}(G^{(1)})\subseteq\{p>10^{2000}\}, \quad q(G^{(1)})\geqslant rac{q(G)}{10^{10^{3000}}} \quad	ext{and}\quad \delta^{(1)}q(G^{(1)})\geqslant  rac{\delta\cdot q(G)}{10^{10^{3000}}}. \end{equation} In particular, we have  egin{equation} \mathcal{R}(H)\subseteq \mathcal{R}(G^{(1)})\subseteq \{p>10^{2000}\} \end{equation} for any $H\preceq G^{(1)}$ by Lemma ef{lem:Trivial}(b).  igskip 
oindent {\it Stage 2: Obtaining a GCD subgraph $G^{(2)}$ with $\mathcal{R}^ lat(G^{(2)})=\emptyset$.} \medskip If $\mathcal{R}^ lat(G^{(1)})
e \emptyset$, then $G^{(1)}$ satisfies the conditions of Proposition ef{prop:IterationStep1}. We then repeatedly apply Proposition ef{prop:IterationStep1} to produce a sequence of GCD subgraphs of $G^{(1)}$ given by \[ G^{(1)}=:G^{(1)}_1\succeq G^{(1)}_2\succeq\cdots \] until we obtain a GCD subgraph $G^{(2)}$ of $G^{(1)}$ which does not satisfy the conditions of Proposition ef{prop:IterationStep1}. Since $\mathcal{R}(G^{(1)}_{i+1})\subsetneq \mathcal{R}(G^{(1)}_i)$ and $\mathcal{R}(G^{(1)})$ is a finite set, this process must indeed terminate after a finite number of steps and produce a GCD graph $G^{(2)}:=(\mu,\mathcal{V}^{(2)},\mathcal{W}^{(2)},\mathcal{E}^{(2)},\mathcal{P}^{(2)},f^{(2)},g^{(2)})\preceq G^{(1)}$ that does not satisfy the conditions of Proposition ef{prop:IterationStep1}. Since $\mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})\subseteq \{p>10^{2000}\}$ by \eqref{eq:R of subgraphs}, it must be the case that \[ \mathcal{R}^ lat(G^{(2)})=\emptyset. \] In addition, Proposition ef{prop:IterationStep1} implies that \[ q(G^{(2)})\geqslant 2^N q(G^{(1)}) \quad	ext{and}\quad \delta^{(2)}q(G^{(2)})\geqslant 2^N\delta^{(1)}\, q(G^{(1)}), \] where \[ N=\#\{p\in\mathcal{P}^{(2)}\setminus\mathcal{P}^{(1)}:f^{(2)}(p)
eq g^{(2)}(p)\}. \] Together with \eqref{eq:G1Quality}, this yields that  egin{equation} q(G^{(2)})\geqslant  rac{2^N}{10^{10^{3000}}} \cdot q(G) \quad	ext{and}\quad \delta^{(2)}q(G^{(2)})\geqslant  rac{2^N}{10^{10^{3000}}} \cdot\delta\cdot q(G). \end{equation} On the other hand, if $\mathcal{R}^ lat(G^{(1)})=\emptyset$, then we simply take $G^{(2)}=G^{(1)}$ and note that \eqref{eq:G2Quality} is trivially satisfied by \eqref{eq:G1Quality}. \medskip This completes Stage 2. The remaining part of the proof deviates according to whether the ratio $q(G^{(2)})/q(G)$ is larger or smaller than $(t/10)^{50}\delta/10^{10^{3000}}$.  igskip 
oindent {\it Case (a): $q(G^{(2)})/q(G)\geqslant (t/10)^{50}\delta/10^{10^{3000}}$.} \smallskip In this case we do not need to keep track of the condition that $L_t(v,w)\geqslant10$ because we have a very large gain in the quality of the new graph. The next stage of the argument is then:  igskip 
oindent {\it Stage 3a: Obtaining a GCD subgraph with} $\mathcal{R}(G^{(3	ext{a})})=\emptyset$. \medskip Notice that if $H\preceq G^{(2)}$, then $\mathcal{R}(H)\subseteq\{p>10^{2000}\}$ by \eqref{eq:R of subgraphs}. Consequently, if $\mathcal{R}(H)
eq\emptyset$, then either Proposition ef{prop:IterationStep1} or Proposition ef{prop:IterationStep2} is applicable to $H$, thus producing a GCD subgraph $H'$ of $H$ such that  egin{equation} \mathcal{R}(H')\subsetneq \mathcal{R}(H) \quad	ext{and}\quad q(H')\geqslant q(H). \end{equation} Since $\mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})$ is finite, starting with $H_1=G^{(2)}$ and iterating the above fact, we can construct a finite sequence of GCD subgraphs \[ G^{(2)}=H_1\succeq H_2\succeq\cdots\succeq H_J=:G^{(3	ext{a})} \] such that \[ \mathcal{R}(G^{(3	ext{a})})=\emptyset \quad 	ext{and}\quad q(G^{(3	ext{a})})\geqslant q(G^{(2)}). \] Applying the assumption that $q(G^{(2)})/q(G)\geqslant (t/10)^{50}\delta/10^{10^{3000}}$, we infer that \[ q(G^{(3	ext{a})})\geqslant \Bigl( rac{t}{10}\Bigr)^{50} rac{\delta}{10^{10^{3000}}} \cdot q(G). \] Hence, the GCD graph $G'=G^{(3	ext{a})}$ satisfies condition ef{prop:Parta} and condition ef{prop:Partd}-ef{prop:Case1} of Proposition ef{prop:BoundOnEdges}, giving the result in this case. (Recall that we may also guarantee conditions ef{prop:Partb} and ef{prop:Partc} of Proposition ef{prop:BoundOnEdges} by feeding our graph into Lemma ef{lem:HighDegreeSubgraph}.) \medskip In order to complete the proof of Proposition ef{prop:BoundOnEdges}, it remains to consider the situation when $q(G^{(2)})/q(G)$ is not large.  igskip 
oindent {\it Case (b): $q(G^{(2)})/q(G)<(t/10)^{50}\delta/10^{10^{3000}}$.} \medskip In this case, the quality increment is small and we must make sure not to lose track of the condition $L_t(v,w)\geqslant10$. For this reason, we perform some cosmetic surgery to our graph before applying Proposition ef{prop:IterationStep2}. This consists of {\it Stage 3b} that we present below.  igskip 
oindent {\it Stage 3b: Removing the effect of primes in $\mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})$ from the anatomical condition $L_t(v,w)\geqslant10$.} \medskip Note that \eqref{eq:G2Quality} implies that \[ \delta^{(2)}\geqslant rac{\delta}{10^{10^{3000}}} \cdot  rac {q(G)}{q(G^{(2)})}\geqslant \Bigl( rac{10}{t}\Bigr)^{50}, \] and that \eq{ 2^N\leqslant 10^{10^{3000}} \cdot  rac{q(G^{(2)})}{q(G)}\leqslant \Bigl( rac{t}{10}\Bigr)^{50}\delta\leqslant t^{50}, } where we recall that \[ N=\#\{p\in\mathcal{P}^{(2)}\setminus\mathcal{P}^{(1)}:f^{(2)}(p)
e g^{(2)}(p)\} \] (here we used the trivial bound $\delta\leqslant 1$). Since $\delta^{(2)}\geqslant (10/t)^{50}$, $\mathcal{R}^ lat(G^{(2)})=\emptyset$, and $L_t(v,w)\geqslant10$ for all $(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}^{(2)}$, it is the case that $G^{(2)}$ satisfies the conditions of Lemma ef{lem:Cosmetic}. Consequently, there exists a GCD subgraph $G^{(3	ext{b})}=(\mu,\mathcal{V}^{(3	ext{b})},\mathcal{W}^{(3	ext{b})},\mathcal{E}^{(3	ext{b})},\mathcal{P}^{(3	ext{b})},f^{(3	ext{b})},g^{(3	ext{b})})$ of $G^{(2)}$ with  egin{align} \mathcal{P}^{(3	ext{b})}&=\mathcal{P}^{(2)},\ q(G^{(3	ext{b})})&\geqslant  rac{q(G^{(2)})}{2}, \end{align} and such that  egin{equation} \sum_{\substack{p|v w/\gcd(v,w)^2\p\geqslant t,\ p
otin \mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})}} rac{1}{p}\geqslant 5 \quad	ext{whenever}\quad (v,w)\in\mathcal{E}^{(3	ext{b})}, \end{equation} We claim that an inequality of the form \eqref{eq:Anat1} holds even if we remove from consideration the primes lying in the set \[ \mathcal{P}^{(2)}_{	ext{diff}}:=\{p\in\mathcal{P}^{(2)}:\,f^{(2)}(p)
e g^{(2)}(p)\}. \] It turns out that we can do this rather crudely, starting from the estimate \[ \sum_{\substack{p|v w/\gcd(v,w)^2\p\geqslant t,\ p\in \mathcal{P}^{(2)}_{	ext{diff}}}} rac{1}{p} \leqslant  rac{\#(\mathcal{P}_{	ext{diff}}^{(2)}\cap\{p\geqslant t\})}{t}. \] Recalling that $t>10^{2000}$ and $\mathcal{P}^{(1)}\subseteq\{p\leqslant10^{2000}\}$, we deduce that  egin{equation} \sum_{\substack{p|v w/\gcd(v,w)^2\p\geqslant t,\ p\in \mathcal{P}^{(2)}_{	ext{diff}}}} rac{1}{p} \leqslant  rac{\#(\mathcal{P}_{	ext{diff}}^{(2)}\setminus\mathcal{P}^{(1)} )}{t}= rac{N}{t}. \end{equation} Since $t\geqslant 10^{2000}$, relation \eqref{eq:N-bound} implies that $N\leqslant 2\log(t^{50})=100\log t<t$, that is to say the right hand side of \eqref{eq:removing P^2_diff} is $\leqslant 1$. As a consequence,  egin{equation} \sum_{\substack{p|v w/\gcd(v,w)^2\ p\geqslant t,\ p
otin \mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})\cup \mathcal{P}^{(2)}_{	ext{diff}}}} rac{1}{p}\geqslant 4 \quad	ext{whenever}\quad (v,w)\in\mathcal{E}^{(3	ext{b})}. \end{equation} Having removed the effect to the condition $L_t(v,w)\geqslant10$ of primes from the sets $\mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})\cup\mathcal{P}_{	ext{diff}}^{(2)}$, we are ready to complete the construction of $G'$ in Case (b).  igskip 
oindent {\it Stage 4b: Obtaining a GCD subgraph with} $\mathcal{R}(G^{(4	ext{b})})=\emptyset$. \medskip We argue as in Stage 3a: for each $H\preceq G^{(3	ext{b})}$, we have $\mathcal{R}(H)\subseteq\{p>10^{2000}\}$ by \eqref{eq:R of subgraphs}. Hence, if $\mathcal{R}(H)
eq\emptyset$, then either Proposition ef{prop:IterationStep1} or Proposition ef{prop:IterationStep2} is applicable to $H$, thus producing a GCD subgraph $H'$ of $H$ such that  egin{equation} \mathcal{R}(H')\subsetneq \mathcal{R}(H),\quad \mathcal{P}_{H'}\subseteq \mathcal{R}(H)\cup \mathcal{P}_H , \quad	ext{and}\quad q(H')\geqslant q(H), \end{equation} where $\mathcal{P}_H$ and $\mathcal{P}_{H'}$ denote the set of primes of $H$ and of $H'$, respectively. Since $\mathcal{R}(G^{(3	ext{b})})$ is finite, starting with $H_1=G^{(3	ext{b})}$ and iterating the above fact, we can construct a finite sequence of GCD subgraphs \[ G^{(3	ext{b})}=H_1\succeq H_2\succeq\cdots\succeq H_J=:G^{(4	ext{b})} \] such that \[ \mathcal{R}(G^{(4	ext{b})})=\emptyset\quad	ext{and}\quad q(G^{(4	ext{b})})\geqslant q(G^{(3	ext{b})}). \] In addition, note that \[ \mathcal{P}^{(4	ext{b})} \subseteq \mathcal{R}(G^{(3	ext{b})})\cup\mathcal{P}^{(3	ext{b})} \subseteq \mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})\cup\mathcal{P}^{(2)}, \] where the second relation follows by fact \eqref{eq:P3b} that $\mathcal{P}^{(3	ext{b})}=\mathcal{P}^{(2)}$. We now verify that if we let \[ G'=G^{(4b)}, \] then condition ef{prop:Partd}-ef{prop:Case2} of Proposition ef{prop:BoundOnEdges} is satisfied. This suffices for the completion of the proof, since $G'$ clearly satisfies condition ef{prop:Parta} of Proposition ef{prop:BoundOnEdges}, and an application of Lemma ef{lem:HighDegreeSubgraph} can also ensure conditions ef{prop:Partb} and ef{prop:Partc}. First of all, note that by \eqref{eq:G3Quality} and \eqref{eq:G2Quality} and $q(G^{(4	ext{b})})\geqslant q(G^{(3	ext{b})})$, we have \[ q(G') = q(G^{(4	ext{b})})\geqslant q(G^{(3	ext{b})})\geqslant  rac{q(G^{(2)})}{2} \geqslant  rac{q(G)}{2\cdot 10^{10^{3000}}}. \] Let $(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}^{(4	ext{b})}$. It remains to check that $L_t(v',w')\geqslant4$, where $v'$ and $w'$ are defined by the relations \[ v=v'\prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}^{(4	ext{b})}}p^{f^{(4	ext{b})}(p)} \quad	ext{and}\quad w=w'\prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}^{(4	ext{b})}}p^{g^{(4	ext{b})}(p)}. \] By the definition of the set $\mathcal{R}(G^{(4	ext{b})})$ and since $\mathcal{R}(G^{(4b)})=\emptyset$, all prime factors of $\gcd(v,w)$ belong to $\mathcal{P}^{(4	ext{b})}$. But for each prime $p\in\mathcal{P}^{(4	ext{b})}$ we have $p^{\min\{f^{(4	ext{b})}(p),g^{(4	ext{b})}(p)\}}\|\gcd(v,w)$. Thus \[ \gcd(v,w) = \prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}^{(4	ext{b})}}p^{\min\{f^{(4	ext{b})}(p),g^{(4	ext{b})}(p)\}}. \] In particular, we must have that \[ \gcd(v',w')=1. \] Now, let $p$ be a prime such that \[ p| rac{vw}{\gcd(v,w)^2}\quad	ext{and}\quad p
mid v'w'. \] Since $p
mid v'w'$ but $p|vw$, we must have $p\in\mathcal{P}^{(4	ext{b})}$, and so $p^{\min\{f^{(4	ext{b})}(p),g^{(4	ext{b})}(p)\}}\|\gcd(v,w)$. In addition, our assumptions that $p
mid v'w'$ and $p|v w/\gcd(v,w)^2$ imply that $f^{(4	ext{b})}(p)
e g^{(4	ext{b})}(p)$. If $p\in\mathcal{P}^{(2)}$, we infer that $p\in \mathcal{P}^{(2)}_{	ext{diff}}$. On the other hand, if $p
otin\mathcal{P}^{(2)}$, then the inclusion $\mathcal{P}^{(4	ext{b})}\subseteq \mathcal{P}^{(2)}\cup\mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})$ implies that $p\in \mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})$. In either case, we have that $p\in\mathcal{P}^{(2)}_{	ext{diff}}\cup\mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})$. Thus, since $\mathcal{E}^{(4	ext{b})}\subseteq\mathcal{E}^{(3	ext{b})}$, we may use the bound \eqref{eq:Anat4}, which gives \[ L_t(v',w')=\sum_{\substack{p|v' w'/\gcd(v',w')^2\ p\geqslant t}} rac{1}{p}\geqslant\sum_{\substack{p|v w/\gcd(v,w)^2\p\geqslant t,\ p
otin \mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})\cup \mathcal{P}^{(2)}_{	ext{diff}}}} rac{1}{p}\geqslant 4. \] In particular, $G'=G^{(4	ext{b})}$ satisfies the conditions of case ef{prop:Partd}-ef{prop:Case2} of Proposition ef{prop:BoundOnEdges}. This completes the proof of Proposition ef{prop:BoundOnEdges} in Case (b) too.

nodes.statement_short: Multi-stage iteration: absorb small primes (Prop. 8.3), then iterate Props. 8.1/8.2 until $\mathcal{R}=\emptyset$. If the gain is small, first apply the cosmetic Lemma 8.4 to keep $L_t(v',w')\ge4$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 8.4
nodes.statement: In this section we establish Lemma \ref{lem:Cosmetic} directly. For brevity, let \[ S(v,w) = \sum_{\substack{p|v w/\gcd(v,w)^2\\p\in \mathcal{R}(G),\ p\geqslant t^{50}}}\frac{1}{p}. \] We have \[ \sum_{(v,w)\in\mathcal{E} } \mu(v)\mu(w) S(v,w) = \sum_{\substack{p\in \mathcal{R}(G) \\ p\geqslant t^{50}}}\frac{1}{p}\cdot \mu\Bigl(\Bigl\{(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}: p|\frac{v w}{\gcd(v,w)^2}\Bigr\}\Bigr) . \] Fix for the moment a prime $p\in\mathcal{R}(G)$.
