But if this were not the case, there would exist a fraction $a/q$ such that $a_j/q_j=a/q$ for infinitely many $j$, so that $|\alpha-a/q|\leqslant \psi(n_j)/n_j\leqslant1/(2n_j)$ for all such $j$. Letting $j\to\infty$, we find that $\alpha=a/q\in\mathbb{Q}$, a contradiction. This completes the proof of \eqref{eq:catlin2}, and hence of Theorem \ref{thm:catlin} in all cases.
nodes.statement_short: Prove $\mathcal{C}\setminus\mathbb{Q}=\mathcal{K}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$, which with Theorem 1 and (1.4) gives Theorem 2.

nodes.name: State claim
nodes.statement: We claim that \eq{ \mathcal{C}\setminus\mathbb{Q}=\mathcal{K}\setminus\mathbb{Q}. } This will immediately complete the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:catlin}(b) by applying Theorem \ref{thm:MainThm}. In addition, Theorem \ref{thm:catlin}(a) will follow from \eqref{DS-BC}.
nodes.statement_short: Claim the limsup sets agree off $\mathbb{Q}$; this finishes via Theorem 1 and (1.4).

nodes.name: C subset K
nodes.statement: Indeed, if $\alpha \in \mathcal{C}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$, then there are infinitely many reduced fractions $a_j/q_j$ such $|\alpha-a_j/q_j|\leqslant\xi(q_j)/q_j$. By the definition of $\xi$, there is some $n_j$ that is a multiple of $q_j$ such that $\xi(q_j)/q_j=\psi(n_j)/n_j$. If we let $m_j=a_j n_j/q_j$, then $|\alpha-m_j/n_j|\leqslant \psi(n_j)/n_j$ for all $j$. Since $\lim_{j\to\infty}q_j=\infty$ and $n_j\geqslant q_j$ for each $j$, we also have that $\lim_{j\to\infty}n_j=\infty$, whence $\alpha \in \mathcal{K}$.

nodes.name: K subset C
nodes.statement: Conversely, let $\alpha \in \mathcal{K}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$. Then there are infinitely many pairs $(m_j,n_j)\in\mathbb{N}^2$ such that $|\alpha-m_j/n_j|\leqslant\psi(n_j)/n_j$. If we let $a_j/q_j$ be the fraction $m_j/n_j$ in reduced form, we also have that $|\alpha-a_j/q_j|\leqslant\psi(n_j)/n_j\leqslant \xi(q_j)/q_j$, where the last inequality follows by noticing that $q_j|n_j$. This shows that $\alpha\in \mathcal{C}$, as long as we can show that infinitely many of the fractions $a_j/q_j$ are distinct. But if this were not the case, there would exist a fraction $a/q$ such that $a_j/q_j=a/q$ for infinitely many $j$, so that $|\alpha-a/q|\leqslant \psi(n_j)/n_j\leqslant1/(2n_j)$ for all such $j$. Letting $j\to\infty$, we find that $\alpha=a/q\in\mathbb{Q}$, a contradiction. This completes the proof of \eqref{eq:catlin2}, and hence of Theorem \ref{thm:catlin} in all cases.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce $m_j/n_j$; infinitely many distinct reductions else $\alpha$ rational.

nodes.name: Simplified set-up
nodes.statement: The purpose of this section is to explain in rough terms the main ideas that go into the proof of our main result. To simplify various technicalities, let us consider the special case where the function $\psi$ satisfies the following conditions: \begin{enumerate} \item $\psi(q)=0$ or $\psi(q)=q^{-c}$ for every $q\in\mathbb{N}$\,; \item $\psi$ is non-zero only on square-free integers $q$\,; \item There exists an infinite sequence $2<x_1<x_2<\dots$ such that: \begin{enumerate} \item $x_j>x_{j-1}^2$\,; \item $\psi$ is supported on $\cup_{i=1}^{\infty}[x_i,2x_i]$\,; \item for each $i$ we have \[ \sum_{q\in [x_i,2x_i]}\frac{\varphi(q)}{q}\psi(q)\in[1,2] \,. \]
nodes.section: 3 Outline of the proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement_short: Restrict to a model case: $\psi\in\{0,q^{-c}\}$, square-free support, lacunary blocks.

nodes.name: Second moment reduction
nodes.statement: In this set-up, it follows from a well-known second moment argument (which will be explained in detail in Section \ref{sec:Prelim}) that to establish the Duffin-Schaeffer conjecture it is sufficient to show that for any $x\in \{x_1,\,x_2,\dots\}$ we have \[ \sum_{\substack{q,r\in\mathcal{S}\\\gcd(q,r)\leqslant M(q,r)}}\frac{\varphi(q)}{q}\cdot \frac{\varphi(r)}{r}\cdot P(q,r)\ll x^{2c}, \] where \begin{align*} \mathcal{S}&:=\{q\in\mathbb{Z}\cap[x,2x] : \psi(q)\neq0\},\\ M(q,r)&:=\max\{q\psi(r),r\psi(q)\}\asymp x^{1-c},\\ P(q,r)&:=\prod_{\substack{p|qr/\gcd(q,r)^2\\ p>M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)}}\Bigl(1+\frac{1}{p}\Bigr). \end{align*} Note that we have the estimate \[ \sum_{q\in \mathcal{S}}\frac{\varphi(q)}{q}\asymp x^{c}\sum_{q\in\mathcal{S}}\frac{\varphi(q)}{q}\psi(q)\asymp x^{c} , \] so the key to the proof is to show that $P(q,r)\ll 1$ on average over $q,r\in\mathcal{S}$. This would then show suitable `approximate independence' of the sets $\mathcal{A}_q$ defined by \eqref{eq:A_q-dfn}. The size of $P(q,r)$ is controlled by small primes dividing exactly one of $q,r$.
nodes.section: 3 Outline of the proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement_short: Second moment argument reduces to $P(q,r)\ll1$ on average.

nodes.name: Threshold reduction
nodes.statement: With this in mind, let us consider separately the contribution from $q,r$ with \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{p|qr/\gcd(q,r)^2\\ p\geqslant t}}\frac{1}{p}\approx 1 \end{equation} for different thresholds $t$ (which we think of as small compared with $x$). A calculation then shows that it is sufficient to show that for each $t\geqslant1$ \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{q,r\in\mathcal{S} \\ \gcd(q,r)\geqslant x^{1-c}/t}}\frac{\varphi(q)}{q}\cdot \frac{\varphi(r)}{r}\ll \frac{x^{2c}}{t}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3 Outline of the proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement_short: Suffices to bound pairs with gcd $\ge x^{1-c}/t$ by $x^{2c}/t$.

nodes.name: Divisor-bound loss
nodes.statement: In particular, we need to understand the structure of a set $\mathcal{S}$ where many of the pairs $(q,r)\in\mathcal{S}^2$ have a large common factor. There are $O(x^c)$ choices of $q\in \mathcal{S}$ weighted by $\varphi(q)/q$. Given $q\in \mathcal{S}$, there are $x^{o(1)}$ divisors of $q$ that are at least $x^{1-c}/t$. In turn, given such a divisor $d$, there are $O(x^c t)$ integers $r\in[x,2x]$ which are a multiple of $d$ (forgetting the constraint $r\in\mathcal{S}$). This gives a bound $t x^{2c+o(1)}$ for the sum in \eqref{eq:jSum}, and so the key problem is to win back a little bit more than the $x^{o(1)}$ factor from the divisor bound. We wish to do this by gaining a structural understanding of sets $\mathcal{S}$ where many pairs have a large GCD. One way that many pairs in $\mathcal{S}$ can have a large GCD is if a positive proportion of elements of $\mathcal{S}$ are a multiple of some fixed divisor $d$. It is natural to ask if this is the only such construction. If we ignore the $\varphi(q)/q$ weights, this leads us to the following prototypical question that we shall refer to as the {\it Model Problem}.
nodes.section: 3 Outline of the proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement_short: Trivial count loses $x^{o(1)}$; leads to the Model Problem.

nodes.name: Model Problem
nodes.statement: \begin{ModelProblem} Let $\mathcal{S}\subseteq[x,2x]$ satisfy $\#\mathcal{S}\asymp x^{c}$ and be such that there are $\#\mathcal{S}^2/100$ pairs $(a_1,a_2)\in\mathcal{S}^2$ with $\gcd(a_1,a_2)>x^{1-c}$. Must it be the case that there is an integer $d\gg x^{1-c}$ which divides $\gg \#\mathcal{S}$ elements of $\mathcal{S}$? \end{ModelProblem}
nodes.section: 3 Outline of the proof of Theorem 1

nodes.name: Model Problem caveat
nodes.statement: It turns out that the answer to this Model Problem as stated is `no', but a technical variant of it that is sufficient for proving Theorem \ref{thm:MainThm} has a positive answer. For the purposes of this section, we will ignore this subtle issue; we will return to it and discuss it in detail in Section \ref{sec:Concluding}.
nodes.section: 3 Outline of the proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement_short: The Model Problem fails as stated; a weighted variant suffices.

nodes.name: Compression strategy
nodes.statement: To attack our Model Problem, we use a `compression' argument, roughly inspired by the papers of Erd\H os-Ko-Rado \cite{erdoskorado} and Dyson \cite{dyson}. We will repeatedly pass to subsets of $\mathcal{S}$ where we have increasing control over whether given primes occur in the GCDs or not, whilst at the same time showing that the size of the original set is controlled in terms of the size of the new set. At the end of the iteration procedure we will then have arrived at a subset which controls the size of $\mathcal{S}$, and where we know that all large GCDs are caused by a fixed divisor. Since the final set then has a very simple GCD structure, we will have enough information to establish \eqref{eq:jSum}.
nodes.section: 3 Outline of the proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement_short: Use an Erdős-Ko-Rado/Dyson style compression argument.

nodes.name: Bipartite set-up
nodes.statement: To enable the iterations, we pass to a bipartite setup. We start out with sets $\mathcal{V}_0=\mathcal{W}_0=\mathcal{S}$. Then, we construct two decreasing sequences of sets $\mathcal{V}_0\supset \mathcal{V}_1\supset\mathcal{V}_2\supset \cdots$ and $\mathcal{W}_0\supset\mathcal{W}_1\supset\mathcal{W}_2\supset \cdots$, as well as a sequence of primes $p_1,p_2,\dots$ such that either $p_j$ divides all elements of $\mathcal{V}_j$, or $p_j$ is coprime to all elements of $\mathcal{V}_j$ (and similarly with $\mathcal{W}_j$). Since $\mathcal{S}$ contains only square-free integers in the simplified set-up of this section, this means that there will be exponents $k_j,\ell_j\in\{0,1\}$ such that $p_j^{k_j}\|v$ for all $v\in\mathcal{V}_j$, and $p_j^{\ell_j}\|w$ for all $w\in\mathcal{W}_j$. Hence, if we let $a_j=p_1^{k_1}\cdots p_j^{k_j}$ and $b_j=p_1^{\ell_1}\cdots p_j^{\ell_j}$, then $a_j$ will divide all elements of $\mathcal{W}_j$ and $b_j$ will divide all elements of $\mathcal{V}_j$.
nodes.section: 3 Outline of the proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement_short: Nested vertex sets with fixed $p_j$-divisibility; $a_j,b_j$ divide them.

nodes.name: Iteration step
nodes.statement: We will construct the sets $\mathcal{V}_1,\mathcal{V}_2,\dots$ and $\mathcal{W}_1,\mathcal{W}_2,\dots$ in an iterative fashion. Assume that after $j$ iterations we have arrived at the sets $\mathcal{V}_j,\mathcal{W}_j\subseteq\mathcal{S}$. We then pick a prime $p_{j+1}$ that is different from $p_1,\dots,p_j$, and that occurs as the prime factor of $\gcd(v,w)$ for some $v\in\mathcal{V}_j$, $w\in\mathcal{W}_j$ with $\gcd(v,w)>x^{1-c}/t$. Our goal is to pass judiciously to subsets $\mathcal{V}_{j+1}\subseteq\mathcal{V}_j$ and $\mathcal{W}_{j+1}\subseteq\mathcal{W}_j$ where either $\mathcal{V}_{j+1}$ is all elements of $\mathcal{V}_j$ that are divisible by $p_{j+1}$, or $\mathcal{V}_{j+1}$ is all elements of $\mathcal{V}_j$ coprime to $p_{j+1}$ (and similarly with $\mathcal{W}_{j+1}$). Since we're assuming that $\mathcal{S}$ contains only square-free integers, we then will completely know the $p_{j+1}$-divisibility of all elements of $\mathcal{V}_{j+1}$ and $\mathcal{W}_{j+1}$, so in particular all GCDs between an element of $\mathcal{V}_{j+1}$ and $\mathcal{W}_{j+1}$ will either be multiple of $p_{j+1}$, or all will be coprime to $p_{j+1}$.
nodes.section: 3 Outline of the proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement_short: Pick a new prime of a large gcd and restrict by its divisibility.

nodes.name: Terminal structure
nodes.statement: Eventually, we will arrive at a pair of sets $(\mathcal{V}_J,\mathcal{W}_J)$ such that every pair $(v,w)\in\mathcal{V}_J\times\mathcal{W}_J$ with $\gcd(v,w)>x^{1-c}/t$ has the property that all prime factors of $\gcd(v,w)$ will lie in the set $\{p_1,\dots,p_J\}$ (and moreover we will ensure that there is at least one such pair). This terminates the iterative procedure. By construction, all elements of $\mathcal{V}=\mathcal{V}_J$ will be divisible by the fixed integer $a=a_J$, and similarly all elements of $\mathcal{W}=\mathcal{W}_J$ will be divisible by the fixed integer $b=b_J$. In addition, if $v\in\mathcal{V}$ and $w\in\mathcal{W}$ has $\gcd(v,w)>x^{1-c}/t$, then in fact $\gcd(v,w)$ will be exactly equal to $\gcd(a,b)$ since we know the $p_j$-divisibility for all elements of $\mathcal{V}$ and $\mathcal{W}$. Thus, $\gcd(a,b)>x^{1-c}/t$ and actually every pair $v\in \mathcal{V}$ and $w\in\mathcal{W}$ has $\gcd(v,w)=\gcd(a,b)$.
nodes.section: 3 Outline of the proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement_short: At the end every large-gcd pair has gcd exactly $\gcd(a,b)$.

nodes.name: Density increment fails
nodes.statement: Naturally, the success of the above strategy depends on improving the `structure' of the pair of sets $(\mathcal{V}_j,\mathcal{W}_j)$ at each stage of the algorithm. This will enable us to control a quantity like the left hand side of \eqref{eq:jSum} in terms of a related quantity for $(\mathcal{V},\mathcal{W})=(\mathcal{V}_J,\mathcal{W}_J)$. An initially appealing choice to measure the `structure' might be \[ \delta_j=\frac{\#\{(v,w)\in\mathcal{V}_j\times\mathcal{W}_j:\, \gcd(v,w)>x^{1-c}/t\}}{\#\mathcal{V}_j\cdot \#\mathcal{W}_j}, \] namely the density of pairs $(v,w)$ with large GCD at stage $j$. Iteratively increasing this quantity would try to mimic a `density increment' strategy such as that used in the proof of Roth's Theorem on arithmetic progressions \cite{roth1,roth2}. Unfortunately, such an argument loses all control over the size of the sets $\mathcal{V}_j,\mathcal{W}_j$, and so we lose control over the sum in \eqref{eq:jSum}.
nodes.section: 3 Outline of the proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement_short: Incrementing edge density alone loses control of set sizes.

nodes.name: Size quantity fails
nodes.statement: An alternative suggestion might be to consider a different quantity which focuses on the size of the sets. Recall that all elements of $\mathcal{V}_j$ are a multiple of $a_j$, all elements of $\mathcal{W}_j$ are a multiple of $b_j$, and that in our final step we have $\gcd(a,b)>x^{1-c}/t$. Thus \al{ \#\mathcal{V}\cdot \#\mathcal{W} &\leqslant \#\{(v,w)\in(\mathbb{Z}\cap[x,2x])^2 : a|v,\ b|w\} \ll \frac{x^2}{ab} \leqslant t^2 x^{2c}\cdot \frac{\gcd(a,b)^2}{ab} , } where we used that $\mathcal{V}=\mathcal{V}_J$ and $\mathcal{W}=\mathcal{W}_J$ are subsets of $[x,2x]$ in \eqref{eq:anatomy2}. Thus, one might try to iteratively increase the quantity \[ \#\mathcal{V}_j\cdot \#\mathcal{W}_j\cdot \frac{a_jb_j}{\gcd(a_j,b_j)^2}. \] This would adequately control \eqref{eq:jSum}, but unfortunately it is not possible to guarantee that this quantity increases at each stage, and so this proposal also fails.
nodes.section: 3 Outline of the proof of Theorem 1

nodes.name: Hybrid quality
nodes.statement: However, the variant \begin{equation} \delta_j^{10}\cdot \#\mathcal{V}_j\cdot \#\mathcal{W}_j \cdot\frac{a_jb_j}{\gcd(a_j,b_j)^2} \end{equation} turns out to (more-or-less) work well. Indeed, if the quantity \eqref{eq:QualityAttempt} increases at each iteration, and at the final iteration all elements of $\mathcal{V}=\mathcal{V}_J$ are a multiple of $a=a_J$, all elements of $\mathcal{W}=\mathcal{W}_J$ are a multiple of $b=b_J$, and all edges come from pairs $(v,w)$ with $\gcd(v,w)=\gcd(a,b)>x^{1-c}/t$, then we find that \begin{equation} \delta_0^{10}\cdot \#\mathcal{S}^2\leqslant \delta_J^{10}\cdot \#\mathcal{V}\cdot \#\mathcal{W}\cdot \frac{ab}{\gcd(a,b)^2} \leqslant \#\mathcal{V}\cdot \#\mathcal{W} \cdot \frac{ab}{\gcd(a,b)^2}\ll t^2x^{2c}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3 Outline of the proof of Theorem 1

nodes.name: Loss of t^12
nodes.statement: We note that in our setup $\#\mathcal{S}\asymp x^{c}$, and that \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{q,r\in\mathcal{S} \\ \gcd(q,r)>x^{1-c}/t}}1=\delta_0\cdot \#\mathcal{S}^2. \end{equation} If it so happens that $\delta_0\leqslant 1/t$, then we trivially obtain \eqref{eq:jSum} (ignoring the $\varphi(q)/q$ weighting) from \eqref{eq:EdgeRewrite}. On the other hand, if $\delta_0\gg 1/t $, then \eqref{eq:IterationBound1} falls short of \eqref{eq:jSum} only by a factor $t^{12}$.
nodes.section: 3 Outline of the proof of Theorem 1

nodes.name: Anatomy gain
nodes.statement: Finally, to win the additional factor of $t^{12}$ we make use of the fact that any edge $(q,r)$ in our graph satisfies \eqref{eq:tThreshold}. The crucial estimate is that \eq{ \#\Bigl\{n<x:\sum_{\substack{p|n\\ p\geqslant t}}\frac{1}{p}\geqslant 1\Bigr\}\ll e^{-t} x . } This was the key idea in the earlier work of Erd\H os \cite{erdos} and Vaaler \cite{vaaler} on the Duffin-Schaeffer conjecture. In our case, our iteration procedure has essentially reduced the proof to a similar situation to their work.
nodes.section: 3 Outline of the proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement_short: Few integers have many prime factors above $t$ (Erdős-Vaaler idea).

nodes.name: Apply anatomy
nodes.statement: Indeed, in \eqref{eq:anatomy2}, we may restrict our attention to pairs $(v,w)$ such that $a|v$, $b|w$ and \eq{ \sum_{\substack{p|vw/\gcd(v,w)^2 \\ p\geqslant t}} \frac{1}{p} \approx 1. } Unless most of the contribution to the above sum of comes from primes in $a$ and $b$, we can apply \eqref{eq:anatomy-gain} to win a factor of size $e^{-t}=o(t^{-12})$ in \eqref{eq:anatomy2}. Finally, if the small primes in $a$ and $b$ do cause a problem, then a more careful analysis of our iteration procedure shows that we actually are able to increase the quantity \eqref{eq:QualityAttempt} by more than $t^{12}$ by the final stage $J$, which also suffices for establishing \eqref{eq:jSum} in this case.
nodes.section: 3 Outline of the proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement_short: Win $e^{-t}$ unless small primes of $a,b$ dominate, then a larger quality gain.

nodes.name: Technicalities
nodes.statement: The above description has ignored several important technicalities; it turns out that the $\varphi(q)/q$ weights are vital for our argument to work (see the discussion in Section \ref{sec:Concluding}). In addition, we do not quite work with \eqref{eq:QualityAttempt} but with a closely related (but more complicated) expression to enable this quantity to increase at each iteration. The iteration procedure of our argument is broken up into different stages. In between two of the principal iterative stages, we perform a certain `clean-up' step at which we allow a small loss in the quantity \eqref{eq:QualityAttempt}. This step is essential in order to keep track of the condition \eqref{eq:anatomy-condition-rough} (which could otherwise become meaningless after too many iterations).
nodes.section: 3 Outline of the proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement_short: The $\varphi(q)/q$ weights and a clean-up step are essential.

nodes.name: Goal
nodes.statement: We wish to prove that \begin{equation} \lambda(\mathcal{A})=1, \end{equation} where $\mathcal{A}=\limsup_{q\to\infty}\mathcal{A}_q$ with $\mathcal{A}_q$ defined by \eqref{eq:A-dfn}.

nodes.name: Split psi
nodes.statement: We first write \[ \psi(q)=\psi_1(q)+\psi_2(q), \qquad\text{where}\qquad \psi_1(q) =\begin{cases} \psi(q)&\text{if}\ \psi(q)>1/2,\\ 0&\text{otherwise} . \end{cases} \] In particular, $\psi_2(q)=\psi(q)$ if $\psi(q)\leqslant 1/2$, and $\psi_2(q)=0$ otherwise.
nodes.statement_short: Split $\psi=\psi_1+\psi_2$ by large and small values.

nodes.name: Large values diverge
nodes.statement: If it so happens that $\sum_{q=1}^\infty \psi_1(q)\varphi(q)/q=\infty$, then we apply Lemma \ref{lem:Large} to $\psi_1$ to find that $\lambda(\limsup_{q\to\infty}\mathcal{B}_q)=1$, where $\mathcal{B}_q$ is defined as $\mathcal{A}_q$ but with $\psi$ replaced by $\psi_1$. This proves \eqref{eq:MainGoal}, since $\psi_1(q)\leqslant \psi(q)$, and so $\mathcal{B}_q\subseteq\mathcal{A}_q$.

nodes.name: WLOG psi <= 1/2
nodes.statement: Therefore we may assume without loss of generality that $\sum_{q=1}^\infty \psi_1(q)\varphi(q)/q<\infty$, and so $\sum_{q=1}^\infty \psi_2(q)\varphi(q)/q=\infty$. Thus, we have reduced Theorem \ref{thm:MainThm} to the case when \[ \psi(q)\leqslant 1/2\quad\text{for all}\ q\geqslant1. \]

nodes.name: Gallagher reduction
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{lem:Gallagher}, the Duffin-Schaeffer conjecture will follow if we prove that $\lambda(\mathcal{A})>0$, since this means $\mathcal{A}$ cannot have measure 0. Note that \begin{equation} \mathcal{A}=\limsup_{q\to\infty}\mathcal{A}_q = \bigcap_{j=1}^{\infty} \bigcup_{q\geqslant j}\mathcal{A}_q . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: By the 0-1 law it suffices to show $\lambda(\mathcal{A})>0$.

nodes.name: Finite window
nodes.statement: Now, let $X$ be a large parameter and fix $Y=Y(X)$ to be minimal such that \[ \sum_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y} \frac{\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q} \in[1,2] . \] (Such a $Y$ exists since $\psi(q)\leqslant 1/2$ for all $q$.) Hence, we see that it suffices to prove that \begin{equation} \lambda\bigg(\bigcup_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y} \mathcal{A}_q\bigg)\gg1 \end{equation} uniformly for all large enough $X$, since this implies that $\lambda(\mathcal{A})>0$ by virtue of \eqref{eq:limsup-rewrite}, and hence Theorem \ref{thm:MainThm} follows.

nodes.name: Counting function Q
nodes.statement: For each $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$, consider the counting function \[ Q(\alpha)=\#\{q\in\mathbb{Z}\cap [X,Y]: \alpha\in\mathcal{A}_q\} = \sum_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y} \mathds{1}_{\mathcal{A}_q}(\alpha). \] We then have \begin{align*} \mathrm{supp}(Q)&=\bigcup_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y}\mathcal{A}_q,\\ \int_0^1 Q(\alpha) \mathrm{d}\alpha &= \sum_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y}\lambda(\mathcal{A}_q) \geqslant \sum_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y} \frac{\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q} \geqslant 1 ,\\ \int_0^1 Q(\alpha)^2 \mathrm{d}\alpha &= \sum_{X\leqslant q,r \leqslant Y}\lambda(\mathcal{A}_q\cap \mathcal{A}_r) . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Define $Q(\alpha)$ and compute its first two moments.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement: Hence, the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality implies that \[ \lambda\bigg(\bigcup_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y}\mathcal{A}_q\bigg)\int_0^1 Q(\alpha)^2\mathrm{d}\alpha \geqslant\Bigl(\int_0^1Q(\alpha)\mathrm{d} \alpha\Bigr)^2\geqslant1. \] Thus, to establish \eqref{eq:Finite}, it is enough to prove that \begin{equation} \sum_{X\leqslant q,r\leqslant Y} \lambda(\mathcal{A}_q\cap \mathcal{A}_r) \ll 1 . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz reduces to the second moment bound (5.5).

nodes.name: Diagonal terms
nodes.statement: The terms with $q=r$ contribute a total \[ \sum_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y}\lambda(\mathcal{A}_q)\leqslant \sum_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y} \frac{2\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q}\leqslant 4, \] and so we only need to consider the contribution of those terms with $q\ne r$.

nodes.name: Apply overlap bound
nodes.statement: Applying Lemma \ref{lem:Pollington}, we see that \[ \lambda(\mathcal{A}_q\cap \mathcal{A}_r)\ll \mathds{1}_{M(q,r)\geqslant \gcd(q,r)}\cdot \frac{\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q}\cdot \frac{\varphi(r)\psi(r)}{r}\cdot \prod_{\substack{p|qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p>M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)}} \left(1+\frac{1}{p}\right) , \] where we recall that \[ M(q,r)=\max\{r\psi(q),q\psi(r)\}. \] Thus, \eqref{eq:2ndmoment-goal} is reduced to showing that \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{X\leqslant q,r\leqslant Y \\ M(q,r)\geqslant\gcd(q,r) }} \frac{\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q} \cdot\frac{\varphi(r)\psi(r)}{r} \prod_{\substack{p|qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p>M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)}}\left(1+\frac{1}{p}\right) \ll 1. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Small products
nodes.statement: To prove this inequality, we divide the range of $q$ and $r$ into convenient subsets. The pairs $(q,r)\in (\mathbb{Z}\cap [X,Y])^2$ with \[ \prod_{\substack{p|qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p>M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)}}\left(1+\frac{1}{p}\right) < e^{100} \] contribute a total of at most \[ e^{100}\bigg(\sum_{q\in [X,Y] } \frac{\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q}\bigg)^2 \leqslant 4e^{100} \] to the right hand side of \eqref{eq:goal}, and so can be ignored.

nodes.name: Large prime sum
nodes.statement: For any other pair $(q,r)$, we see that \[ e^{100} \leqslant \prod_{\substack{p|qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p>M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)}}\left(1+\frac{1}{p}\right) \leqslant \exp\Bigl(\sum_{\substack{p|qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p>M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)}}\frac{1}{p}\Bigr), \] so certainly we have \[ \sum_{p|qr/\gcd(q,r)^2}\frac{1}{p} \geqslant 100. \]

nodes.name: Choose j
nodes.statement: For any such pair, we let $j=j(q,r)$ be the largest integer such that \[ \sum_{\substack{p| qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p\geqslant \exp\exp(j)}} \frac{1}{p} \geqslant 10. \] Since $j$ is chosen maximally, we have \[ \sum_{\substack{p| qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p\geqslant \exp\exp(j+1)}} \frac{1}{p} <10 . \]
nodes.statement_short: Let $j$ be maximal with prime sum above $\exp\exp(j)$ at least 10.

nodes.name: Mertens bound
nodes.statement: Mertens' theorem then implies that \[ \sum_{\substack{p| qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p\geqslant \exp\exp(j)}} \frac{1}{p}=\sum_{\substack{p| qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ \exp\exp(j)\leqslant p <\exp\exp(j+1)}} \frac{1}{p}+\sum_{\substack{p| qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p\geqslant \exp\exp(j+1)}} \frac{1}{p} \ll 1 . \] Therefore \als{ \prod_{\substack{p| qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p>M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)}}\left(1+\frac{1}{p}\right) &\ll \prod_{M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)<p\leqslant \exp\exp(j)} \left(1+\frac{1}{p}\right) \\ &\ll\begin{cases} 1&\text{if}\ M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)\geqslant \exp\exp(j),\\ e^j &\text{otherwise}, \end{cases} } where we used again Mertens' theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Mertens bounds the product by $e^j$ or $O(1)$.

nodes.name: Discard bounded pairs
nodes.statement: As above, those pairs with \[ \prod_{\substack{p| qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p>M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)}}\left(1+\frac{1}{p}\right)\ll 1 \] make an acceptable contribution to \eqref{eq:goal}. Therefore we only need to consider pairs $(q,r)$ with $M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)< \exp\exp(j)$.

nodes.name: Apply Proposition 5.4
nodes.statement: We have thus reduced \eqref{eq:goal} to showing that \begin{equation} \sum_{j\geqslant 0} e^j \sum_{(q,r)\in \mathcal{E}_{\exp\exp(j)}} \frac{\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q}\cdot \frac{\varphi(r)\psi(r)}{r} \ll 1, \end{equation} where $\mathcal{E}_t$ is defined by \eqref{eq:E_t}. To prove \eqref{eq:goal2}, we apply Proposition \ref{prop:GCD}, which shows that the inner sum is $O(1/\exp\exp(j))$. Since the sum of $e^j/\exp\exp(j)$ over $j\geqslant 0$ converges, this completes the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:MainThm}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduced to (5.7), which follows from Proposition 5.4.

nodes.name: Goal
nodes.statement: Recall the notation $\psi$, $M(q,r)$, $L_t(a,b)$, $X$, $Y$ and $\mathcal{E}_t$ of Proposition \ref{prop:GCD}. We wish to show that \begin{equation} \sum_{(v_1,v_2)\in \mathcal{E}_t} \frac{\varphi(v_1)\psi(v_1)}{v_1}\cdot \frac{\varphi(v_2)\psi(v_2)}{v_2} \ll \frac{1}{t} . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Goal: the weighted sum over $\mathcal{E}_t$ is $\ll1/t$.

nodes.name: Measure and vertices
nodes.statement: Let $\mu$ be the measure on $\mathbb{N}$ defined by $\mu(v):=\psi(v)\varphi(v)/v$ and let $\mathcal{V}=\mathbb{Z}\cap[X,Y]$, so that \[ \mu(\mathcal{V})=\sum_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y}\frac{\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q}\in[1,2]. \]

nodes.name: Build GCD graph
nodes.statement: Now define $\mathcal{E}=\mathcal{E}_t$ to be as in Proposition \ref{prop:GCD}. We see that $(\mathcal{V},\mathcal{V},\mathcal{E})$ forms a bipartite graph with vertex sets two copies of $\mathcal{V}$ and edge set $\mathcal{E}$. We now turn this bipartite graph into a GCD graph $G=(\mu,\mathcal{V},\mathcal{V},\mathcal{E},\emptyset,f_\emptyset,g_\emptyset)$ by attaching trivial multiplicative data to the bipartite graph (here $f_\emptyset$ and $g_\emptyset$ are viewed as two copies of the function of the empty set to $\mathbb{Z}_{\geqslant 0}$).
nodes.statement_short: Form the GCD graph with trivial multiplicative data.

nodes.name: Apply Proposition 6.3
nodes.statement: Since $0<\mu(\mathcal{V})\ll 1$, Proposition \ref{prop:Graph} now applies, showing that \[ \mu(\mathcal{E}_t)\ll 1/t. \] This completes the proof.

nodes.name: Rankin's trick
nodes.statement: We may assume that $t$ is large enough, since the result is trivial when $t$ is bounded. Set $T=t^{e^{c-1}}$, so that $\sum_{t\leqslant p<T}1/p \leqslant c-1/2$ by Mertens' theorem. Hence \begin{equation} \#\bigg\{n\leqslant x:\sum_{\substack{p|n\\ p\geqslant t}}\frac{1}{p} \geqslant c \bigg\} \leqslant \#\bigg\{n\leqslant x: \sum_{\substack{p|n\\ p\geqslant T}}\frac{1}{p} \geqslant 1/2 \bigg\} \leqslant e^{-T} \sum_{n\leqslant x} \prod_{\substack{p|n\\ p\geqslant T}} e^{2T/p} . \end{equation}
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph
nodes.statement_short: Mertens and Rankin's trick bound the count by a multiplicative sum.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 7.2
nodes.statement:
We wish to apply Lemma ef{lem:Tenenbaum} when $f$ is the multiplicative function with $f(p^
u)=e^{2T/p}$ for $p\geqslant T$ and all $
u\geqslant 1$, and $f(p^
u)=1$ for $p<T$. In particular, $f(p^
u)\leqslant e^2\leqslant 8$ for all prime powers $p^
u$, so that $f\leqslant 	au_8$. Thus \[ \sum_{n\leqslant x} \prod_{p|n,\ p\geqslant T} e^{2T/p} = \sum_{n\leqslant x} f(n) \ll x \cdot \exp\Big\{\sum_{p\leqslant x}  rac{f(p)-1}{p}\Big\} = x \cdot \exp\Big\{\sum_{T\leqslant p\leqslant x}  rac{e^{2T/p}-1}{p}\Big\} . \]
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Since $e^{2T/p}=1+O(T/p)$ for $p\geqslant T$, and $\sum_{p\geqslant T} T/p^2\ll1$, the sum of $(e^{2T/p}-1)/p$ over $p\in[T,x]$ is $O(1)$. We thus conclude that \[ \#\Big\{n\leqslant x:\sum_{\substack{p|n\\ p\geqslant t}}\frac{1}{p} \geqslant c \Big\}\ll e^{-T}x. \] Since $T=t^{e^{c-1}}$, the lemma has been proven.
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph
nodes.statement_short: The prime sum is $O(1)$, giving $\ll e^{-T}x$.

nodes.name: Set up G
nodes.statement: Fix $t\geqslant1$ and let $G$ be the GCD graph of Proposition \ref{prop:Graph} with set of edges $\mathcal{E}\subseteq\mathcal{E}_t$ (where $\mathcal{E}_t$ is defined in Proposition \ref{prop:GCD}), weight $\mu(v)=\psi(v)\varphi(v)/v$ and edge density $\delta$.
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph

nodes.name: WLOG delta large
nodes.statement: If $\delta\ll 1/t$, then $\mu(\mathcal{E})\ll 1/t$ and so we are done. Therefore we may assume that \[ \delta\geqslant 1/t\quad\text{and}\quad t>10^{2000}. \] Note that this implies that \[ t\geqslant 10\delta^{-1/50}. \]
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph

nodes.name: Apply Proposition 7.1
nodes.statement: We apply Proposition \ref{prop:BoundOnEdges} to $G$ to find a GCD subgraph $G'=(\mu,\mathcal{V}',\mathcal{W}',\mathcal{E}',\mathcal{P}',f',g')$ of $G$ with edge density $\delta'$ satisfying either case \ref{prop:Partd}-\ref{prop:Case1} or \ref{prop:Partd}-\ref{prop:Case2} of its statement. In addition, we have that: \begin{enumerate} \item $\mathcal{R}(G')=\emptyset$; \item $\mu(\Gamma_{G'}(v))\geqslant(9\delta'/10)\mu(\mathcal{W}')$ for all $v\in\mathcal{V}'$; \item $\mu(\Gamma_{G'}(w))\geqslant(9\delta'/10)\mu(\mathcal{V}')$ for all $w\in\mathcal{W}'$.
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph

nodes.name: Define a and b
nodes.statement: Set \[ a:=\prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}'}p^{f'(p)} \quad\text{and}\quad b:=\prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}'}p^{g'(p)}. \] The definition of a GCD graph implies that \[ a|v\quad\text{for all}\ v\in\mathcal{V}', \qquad b|w\quad \text{for all}\ w\in\mathcal{W}'. \] Moreover, since $\mathcal{R}(G')=\emptyset$, and $p^{\min\{f'(p),g'(p)\}}\|\gcd(v,w)$ for all $(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}'$, we have that \[ \gcd(v,w)=\gcd(a,b) \quad\text{for all}\quad(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}'. \]
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph

nodes.name: Bound q(G')
nodes.statement: Now, note that \[ \prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}'}p^{|f'(p)-g'(p)|} = \prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}'}p^{\max\{f'(p),g'(p)\}-\min\{f'(p),g'(p)\}}= \frac{\mathrm{lcm}(a,b)}{\gcd(a,b)} = \frac{ab}{\gcd(a,b)^2} , \] as well as \[ \prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}'}\frac{1}{(1-\mathds{1}_{f'(p)=g'(p)\geqslant1}/p)^2(1-1/p^{31/30})^{10}} \ll \prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}'}\frac{1}{(1-\mathds{1}_{f'(p)=g'(p)\geqslant1}/p)^2} \leqslant \frac{ab}{\varphi(a)\varphi(b)} . \] Consequently, from the definition of $q(\cdot)$, we find \begin{align} q(G') &= (\delta')^{10}\mu(\mathcal{V}')\mu(\mathcal{W}') \prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}'} \frac{p^{|f'(p)-g'(p)|}}{(1-\mathds{1}_{f'(p)=g'(p)\geqslant1}/p)^2(1-1/p^{31/30})^{10}}\nonumber\\ & \ll (\delta')^{10} \mu(\mathcal{V}')\mu(\mathcal{W}') \frac{ab}{\gcd(a,b)^2} \cdot \frac{ab}{\varphi(a)\varphi(b)}\nonumber \\ &= (\delta')^{9}\mu(\mathcal{E}') \frac{ab}{\gcd(a,b)^2} \cdot \frac{ab}{\varphi(a)\varphi(b)} . \end{align} Proposition \ref{prop:BoundOnEdges} offers a lower bound on $q(G')/q(G)$. Since \[ q(G) = \delta^{10} \mu(\mathcal{V})\mu(\mathcal{V})= \delta^{9}\mu(\mathcal{E}), \] we can obtain an upper bound on the size of $\mu(\mathcal{E})$ by estimating $q(G')$ from above.
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph

nodes.name: Bound psi on edges
nodes.statement: Note that \[ \mathcal{E}'\subseteq\mathcal{E} \subseteq\{(v,w)\in\mathcal{V}\times\mathcal{V}: M(v,w)\leqslant t\cdot \gcd(v,w)\}, \] where we recall that $M(v,w)=\max\{v\psi(w),w\psi(v)\}$. Since $\gcd(v,w)=\gcd(a,b)$ for all $(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}'$, we infer that \[ \psi(v)\leqslant \frac{t\cdot \gcd(a,b)}{w} \quad\text{and}\quad \psi(w)\leqslant \frac{t\cdot \gcd(a,b)}{v} \quad\text{for all}\quad (v,w)\in\mathcal{E}'. \]
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph

nodes.name: Largest neighbours
nodes.statement: The vertex sets $\mathcal{V}',\mathcal{W}'$ are finite sets of positive integers. For each $v\in\mathcal{V}'$, let $w_{\max}(v)$ be the largest integer in $\mathcal{W}'$ such that $(v,w_{\max}(v))\in\mathcal{E}'$. (This quantity is well-defined in virtue of property (b) above. In addition, we emphasise to the reader that `largest' refers to the size of elements as positive integers, and does not depend on the measure $\mu$.) Similarly, for each $w\in\mathcal{W}'$, let $v_{\max}(w)$ be the largest element of $\mathcal{V}'$ such that $(v_{\max}(w),w)\in\mathcal{E}'$. Consequently, \begin{equation} \psi(v)\leqslant \frac{t\cdot \gcd(a,b)}{w_{\max}(v)} \quad\text{and}\quad \psi(w)\leqslant \frac{t\cdot \gcd(a,b)}{v_{\max}(w)} \quad\text{for all}\quad v\in \mathcal{V}',\,w\in\mathcal{W}'. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph

nodes.name: Restrict to E''
nodes.statement: Now, let $w_0$ be the largest integer in $\mathcal{W}'$ and $\mathcal{E}''=\{(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}': (v,w_0)\in\mathcal{E}'\}$. We then have \begin{equation} w_{\max}(v)=w_0 \quad\text{for all}\quad(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}'' . \end{equation} In addition, since $G'$ satisfies conditions (b) and (c) in the statement of Proposition \ref{prop:BoundOnEdges}, we have \[ \mu(\mathcal{E}'') =\sum_{v\in \Gamma_{G'}(w_0)}\mu(v)\mu(\Gamma_{G'}(v)) \geqslant \mu(\Gamma_{G'}(w_0))\cdot \frac{9\delta'\mu(\mathcal{W}')}{10} \geqslant \bigg(\frac{9\delta'}{10}\bigg)^2 \mu(\mathcal{V}')\mu(\mathcal{W}')\geqslant \frac{\delta'\mu(\mathcal{E}')}{2} . \]
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph
nodes.statement_short: Edges at neighbours of $w_0$ carry a $\delta'/2$ fraction.

nodes.name: Reciprocal sum bound
nodes.statement: Substituting this bound into \eqref{eq:QG'Bound}, we find \begin{equation} q(G') \ll (\delta')^{8} \mu(\mathcal{E}'') \frac{a b}{\varphi(a)\varphi(b)}\cdot \frac{a b}{\gcd(a,b)^2} \leqslant \mu(\mathcal{E}'') \frac{ab}{\gcd(a,b)^2} \cdot \frac{ab}{\varphi(a)\varphi(b)} . \end{equation} Here we used the trivial bound $\delta'\leqslant 1$ in the second inequality. In addition, \als{ \mu(\mathcal{E}'') = \sum_{(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}''} \frac{\psi(v)\varphi(v)}{v} \cdot \frac{\psi(w)\varphi(w)}{w} . } Since $a|v$ and $b|w$, we have $\varphi(v)/v\leqslant \varphi(a)/a$ and $\varphi(w)/w\leqslant \varphi(b)/b$. Therefore \[ \mu(\mathcal{E}'')\leqslant \frac{\varphi(a)\varphi(b)}{a b}\sum_{(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}''}\psi(v)\psi(w). \] Together with \eqref{psi ub}, \eqref{eq:w0} and \eqref{eq:q(G') bound}, this implies that \begin{equation} q(G') \ll t^2ab \sum_{(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}''} \frac{1}{v_{\max}(w) w_0} \leqslant t^2ab \sum_{(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}'} \frac{1}{v_{\max}(w) w_0} . \end{equation} We now split our argument depending on whether \ref{prop:Partd}-\ref{prop:Case1} or \ref{prop:Partd}-\ref{prop:Case2} of Proposition \ref{prop:BoundOnEdges} holds.
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph

nodes.name: Case (d)(i)
nodes.statement: \textit{Case 1: \ref{prop:Partd}-\ref{prop:Case1} of Proposition \ref{prop:BoundOnEdges} holds.} \medskip In this case we have $q(G')\gg \delta t^{50} q(G)$. Writing $v=v' a$ and $w=w' b$, we find that \begin{align*} \sum_{(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}'} \frac{1}{v_{\max}(w) w_0} &\leqslant \sum_{w'\leqslant w_0/b}\frac{1}{ w_0 v_{\max}(b w')} \sum_{v'\leqslant v_{\max}(b w')/a}1\\ &\leqslant \sum_{w'\leqslant w_0/b}\frac{1}{ w_0 v_{\max}(b w')}\cdot \frac{v_{\max}(bw')}{a} \\ &\leqslant \frac{1}{ab} . \end{align*} Together with \eqref{eq:G'Quality}, this implies that \[ q(G')\ll t^2. \] Since $q(G')\gg \delta t^{50} q(G)$ in this case, and since $\delta \geqslant 1/t$, this gives \[ \mu(\mathcal{E}) = \delta^{-9}q(G) \ll \delta^{-10}t^{-50}q(G')\ll \frac{1}{\delta^{10}t^{48}} \ll \frac{1}{t} . \] This establishes Proposition \ref{prop:Graph} in this case.
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph

nodes.name: Case (d)(ii)
nodes.statement: \textit{Case 2: \ref{prop:Partd}-\ref{prop:Case2} of Proposition \ref{prop:BoundOnEdges} holds.} \medskip Write $v=v' a$ and $w=w' b$. In this case \begin{equation} L_t(v',w')\geqslant 4\quad\text{whenever}\quad(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}'. \end{equation} We also have $q(G')\gg q(G)$. From \eqref{eq:L_t-lowerbound}, we see that either \[ \sum_{p|v',\,p\geqslant t}\frac{1}{p}\geqslant 2 \quad\text{or} \quad \sum_{p|w',\,p\geqslant t}\frac{1}{p}\geqslant 2 \] whenever $(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}'$. Consequently, \als{ \sum_{(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}'} \frac{1}{v_{\max}(w) w_0} &\leqslant \mathop{\sum\sum}_{\substack{w'\leqslant w_0/b,\ v'\leqslant v_{\max}(b w')/a\\ \sum_{p|v' w',\,p\geqslant t}1/p\geqslant 4}} \frac{1}{v_{\max}(b w') w_0} \\ &\leqslant S_1+S_2, } where \begin{align*} S_1&=\mathop{\sum\sum}_{\substack{w'\leqslant w_0/b,\ v'\leqslant v_{\max}(b w')/a\\ \sum_{p|v',\,p\geqslant t}1/p\geqslant 2}} \frac{1}{v_{\max}(b w') w_0} ,\\ S_2&=\mathop{\sum\sum}_{\substack{w'\leqslant w_0/b,\ v'\leqslant v_{\max}(b w')/a\\ \sum_{p|w',\,p\geqslant t}1/p\geqslant 2}} \frac{1}{v_{\max}(b w') w_0} . \end{align*} For $S_1$, we note that \als{ S_1&\leqslant \sum_{w'\leqslant w_0/b} \frac{1}{w_0v_{\max}(b w')} \sum_{\substack{v'\leqslant v_{\max}(b w')/a \\ \sum_{p|v',\,p\geqslant t}1/p\geqslant 2}} 1\\ &\ll \sum_{w'\leqslant w_0/b} \frac{1}{w_0v_{\max}(b w')} \cdot \frac{v_{\max}(b w')/a}{t^2e^t} \\ &\leqslant \frac{1}{ab t^2e^t} } by Lemma \ref{lem:Anatomy}, since $\exp(t^e)\gg\exp(t)t^2$. Similarly for $S_2$, we find that \als{ S_2&\leqslant\sum_{\substack{w'\leqslant w_0/b \\ \sum_{p|w',\,p\geqslant t}1/p\geqslant 2}} \frac{1}{w_0v_{\max}(b w')} \sum_{v'\leqslant v_{\max}(b w')/a}1\\ &\leqslant \sum_{\substack{w'\leqslant w_0/b \\ \sum_{p|w',\,p\geqslant t}1/p\geqslant 2}} \frac{1}{aw_0} \\ &\ll \frac{1}{ab t^2e^t} , } by applying Lemma \ref{lem:Anatomy} once again. Substituting these bounds into \eqref{eq:G'Quality}, we conclude that \[ q(G') \ll e^{-t}. \] Since we have $q(G)\ll q(G')$ and $\delta\geqslant 1/t$, this gives \[ \mu(\mathcal{E}) = \delta^{-9}q(G) \ll t^{9} q(G')\ll t^{9} e^{-t} \ll 1/t. \] This establishes Proposition \ref{prop:Graph} in all cases.
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph
nodes.statement_short: Use $L_t(v',w')\ge4$ and Lemma 7.3 to get $q(G')\ll e^{-t}$.

nodes.name: Open case 2
nodes.statement: \textit{Case 2: \ref{prop:Partd}-\ref{prop:Case2} of Proposition \ref{prop:BoundOnEdges} holds.} \medskip Write $v=v' a$ and $w=w' b$. In this case \begin{equation} L_t(v',w')\geqslant 4\quad\text{whenever}\quad(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}'. \end{equation} We also have $q(G')\gg q(G)$.
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph

nodes.name: Split S1 + S2
nodes.statement: From \eqref{eq:L_t-lowerbound}, we see that either \[ \sum_{p|v',\,p\geqslant t}\frac{1}{p}\geqslant 2 \quad\text{or} \quad \sum_{p|w',\,p\geqslant t}\frac{1}{p}\geqslant 2 \] whenever $(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}'$. Consequently, \als{ \sum_{(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}'} \frac{1}{v_{\max}(w) w_0} &\leqslant \mathop{\sum\sum}_{\substack{w'\leqslant w_0/b,\ v'\leqslant v_{\max}(b w')/a\\ \sum_{p|v' w',\,p\geqslant t}1/p\geqslant 4}} \frac{1}{v_{\max}(b w') w_0} \\ &\leqslant S_1+S_2, } where \begin{align*} S_1&=\mathop{\sum\sum}_{\substack{w'\leqslant w_0/b,\ v'\leqslant v_{\max}(b w')/a\\ \sum_{p|v',\,p\geqslant t}1/p\geqslant 2}} \frac{1}{v_{\max}(b w') w_0} ,\\ S_2&=\mathop{\sum\sum}_{\substack{w'\leqslant w_0/b,\ v'\leqslant v_{\max}(b w')/a\\ \sum_{p|w',\,p\geqslant t}1/p\geqslant 2}} \frac{1}{v_{\max}(b w') w_0} . \end{align*}
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph
nodes.statement_short: One of $v',w'$ has prime sum $\ge2$; split into $S_1,S_2$.

nodes.name: Bound S1
nodes.statement: For $S_1$, we note that \als{ S_1&\leqslant \sum_{w'\leqslant w_0/b} \frac{1}{w_0v_{\max}(b w')} \sum_{\substack{v'\leqslant v_{\max}(b w')/a \\ \sum_{p|v',\,p\geqslant t}1/p\geqslant 2}} 1\\ &\ll \sum_{w'\leqslant w_0/b} \frac{1}{w_0v_{\max}(b w')} \cdot \frac{v_{\max}(b w')/a}{t^2e^t} \\ &\leqslant \frac{1}{ab t^2e^t} } by Lemma \ref{lem:Anatomy}, since $\exp(t^e)\gg\exp(t)t^2$.
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph

nodes.name: Bound S2
nodes.statement: Similarly for $S_2$, we find that \als{ S_2&\leqslant\sum_{\substack{w'\leqslant w_0/b \\ \sum_{p|w',\,p\geqslant t}1/p\geqslant 2}} \frac{1}{w_0v_{\max}(b w')} \sum_{v'\leqslant v_{\max}(b w')/a}1\\ &\leqslant \sum_{\substack{w'\leqslant w_0/b \\ \sum_{p|w',\,p\geqslant t}1/p\geqslant 2}} \frac{1}{aw_0} \\ &\ll \frac{1}{ab t^2e^t} , } by applying Lemma \ref{lem:Anatomy} once again.
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Substituting these bounds into \eqref{eq:G'Quality}, we conclude that \[ q(G') \ll e^{-t}. \] Since we have $q(G)\ll q(G')$ and $\delta\geqslant 1/t$, this gives \[ \mu(\mathcal{E}) = \delta^{-9}q(G) \ll t^{9} q(G')\ll t^{9} e^{-t} \ll 1/t. \] This establishes Proposition \ref{prop:Graph} in all cases.
nodes.section: 7 Reduction to a good GCD subgraph

nodes.name: Reduction to (a) and (d)
nodes.statement: We will construct the required subgraph $G'$ in several stages. It suffices to produce a GCD subgraph $G'$ of $G$ satisfying only conclusions $(a)$ and $(d)$ of Proposition \ref{prop:BoundOnEdges}, since an application of Lemma \ref{lem:HighDegreeSubgraph} then produces a GCD subgraph satisfying all the conclusions.
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions
nodes.statement_short: Suffices to get (a) and (d); Lemma 8.5 then gives (b),(c).

nodes.name: Stage 1: small primes
nodes.statement: \textit{Stage 1: Obtaining a GCD subgraph $G^{(1)}$ with $\mathcal{R}(G^{(1)})\subseteq \{p> 10^{2000}\}$.} \medskip Since $G$ has set of primes equal to the empy set, we may apply Proposition \ref{prop:SmallPrimes} to $G$ to produce a GCD subgraph $G^{(1)}=(\mu,\mathcal{V}^{(1)},\mathcal{W}^{(1)},\mathcal{E}^{(1)},\mathcal{P}^{(1)},f^{(1)},g^{(1)})$ of $G$ with edge density $\delta^{(1)}$ and for which \begin{equation} \mathcal{R}(G^{(1)})\subseteq\{p>10^{2000}\}, \quad q(G^{(1)})\geqslant\frac{q(G)}{10^{10^{3000}}} \quad\text{and}\quad \delta^{(1)}q(G^{(1)})\geqslant \frac{\delta\cdot q(G)}{10^{10^{3000}}}. \end{equation} In particular, we have \begin{equation} \mathcal{R}(H)\subseteq \mathcal{R}(G^{(1)})\subseteq \{p>10^{2000}\} \end{equation} for any $H\preceq G^{(1)}$ by Lemma \ref{lem:Trivial}(b).
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions

nodes.name: Stage 2: empty R-flat
nodes.statement: {\it Stage 2: Obtaining a GCD subgraph $G^{(2)}$ with $\mathcal{R}^\flat(G^{(2)})=\emptyset$.} \medskip If $\mathcal{R}^\flat(G^{(1)})\ne \emptyset$, then $G^{(1)}$ satisfies the conditions of Proposition \ref{prop:IterationStep1}. We then repeatedly apply Proposition \ref{prop:IterationStep1} to produce a sequence of GCD subgraphs of $G^{(1)}$ given by \[ G^{(1)}=:G^{(1)}_1\succeq G^{(1)}_2\succeq\cdots \] until we obtain a GCD subgraph $G^{(2)}$ of $G^{(1)}$ which does not satisfy the conditions of Proposition \ref{prop:IterationStep1}. Since $\mathcal{R}(G^{(1)}_{i+1})\subsetneq \mathcal{R}(G^{(1)}_i)$ and $\mathcal{R}(G^{(1)})$ is a finite set, this process must indeed terminate after a finite number of steps and produce a GCD graph $G^{(2)}:=(\mu,\mathcal{V}^{(2)},\mathcal{W}^{(2)},\mathcal{E}^{(2)},\mathcal{P}^{(2)},f^{(2)},g^{(2)})\preceq G^{(1)}$ that does not satisfy the conditions of Proposition \ref{prop:IterationStep1}. Since $\mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})\subseteq \{p>10^{2000}\}$ by \eqref{eq:R of subgraphs}, it must be the case that \[ \mathcal{R}^\flat(G^{(2)})=\emptyset. \] In addition, Proposition \ref{prop:IterationStep1} implies that \[ q(G^{(2)})\geqslant 2^N q(G^{(1)}) \quad\text{and}\quad \delta^{(2)}q(G^{(2)})\geqslant 2^N\delta^{(1)}\, q(G^{(1)}), \] where \[ N=\#\{p\in\mathcal{P}^{(2)}\setminus\mathcal{P}^{(1)}:f^{(2)}(p)\neq g^{(2)}(p)\}. \] Together with \eqref{eq:G1Quality}, this yields that \begin{equation} q(G^{(2)})\geqslant \frac{2^N}{10^{10^{3000}}} \cdot q(G) \quad\text{and}\quad \delta^{(2)}q(G^{(2)})\geqslant \frac{2^N}{10^{10^{3000}}} \cdot\delta\cdot q(G). \end{equation} On the other hand, if $\mathcal{R}^\flat(G^{(1)})=\emptyset$, then we simply take $G^{(2)}=G^{(1)}$ and note that \eqref{eq:G2Quality} is trivially satisfied by \eqref{eq:G1Quality}. \medskip This completes Stage 2. The remaining part of the proof deviates according to whether the ratio $q(G^{(2)})/q(G)$ is larger or smaller than $(t/10)^{50}\delta/10^{10^{3000}}$.
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions

nodes.name: Iterate Proposition 8.1
nodes.statement: {\it Stage 2: Obtaining a GCD subgraph $G^{(2)}$ with $\mathcal{R}^\flat(G^{(2)})=\emptyset$.} \medskip If $\mathcal{R}^\flat(G^{(1)})\ne \emptyset$, then $G^{(1)}$ satisfies the conditions of Proposition \ref{prop:IterationStep1}. We then repeatedly apply Proposition \ref{prop:IterationStep1} to produce a sequence of GCD subgraphs of $G^{(1)}$ given by \[ G^{(1)}=:G^{(1)}_1\succeq G^{(1)}_2\succeq\cdots \] until we obtain a GCD subgraph $G^{(2)}$ of $G^{(1)}$ which does not satisfy the conditions of Proposition \ref{prop:IterationStep1}. Since $\mathcal{R}(G^{(1)}_{i+1})\subsetneq \mathcal{R}(G^{(1)}_i)$ and $\mathcal{R}(G^{(1)})$ is a finite set, this process must indeed terminate after a finite number of steps and produce a GCD graph $G^{(2)}:=(\mu,\mathcal{V}^{(2)},\mathcal{W}^{(2)},\mathcal{E}^{(2)},\mathcal{P}^{(2)},f^{(2)},g^{(2)})\preceq G^{(1)}$ that does not satisfy the conditions of Proposition \ref{prop:IterationStep1}. Since $\mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})\subseteq \{p>10^{2000}\}$ by \eqref{eq:R of subgraphs}, it must be the case that \[ \mathcal{R}^\flat(G^{(2)})=\emptyset. \]
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions

nodes.name: Stage 2 quality
nodes.statement: In addition, Proposition \ref{prop:IterationStep1} implies that \[ q(G^{(2)})\geqslant 2^N q(G^{(1)}) \quad\text{and}\quad \delta^{(2)}q(G^{(2)})\geqslant 2^N\delta^{(1)}\, q(G^{(1)}), \] where \[ N=\#\{p\in\mathcal{P}^{(2)}\setminus\mathcal{P}^{(1)}:f^{(2)}(p)\neq g^{(2)}(p)\}. \] Together with \eqref{eq:G1Quality}, this yields that \begin{equation} q(G^{(2)})\geqslant \frac{2^N}{10^{10^{3000}}} \cdot q(G) \quad\text{and}\quad \delta^{(2)}q(G^{(2)})\geqslant \frac{2^N}{10^{10^{3000}}} \cdot\delta\cdot q(G). \end{equation}
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions

nodes.name: Trivial case
nodes.statement: On the other hand, if $\mathcal{R}^\flat(G^{(1)})=\emptyset$, then we simply take $G^{(2)}=G^{(1)}$ and note that \eqref{eq:G2Quality} is trivially satisfied by \eqref{eq:G1Quality}.
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions

nodes.name: Split on gain
nodes.statement: This completes Stage 2. The remaining part of the proof deviates according to whether the ratio $q(G^{(2)})/q(G)$ is larger or smaller than $(t/10)^{50}\delta/10^{10^{3000}}$.
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions
nodes.statement_short: Split according to the size of $q(G^{(2)})/q(G)$.

nodes.name: Case (a): large gain
nodes.statement: {\it Case (a): $q(G^{(2)})/q(G)\geqslant (t/10)^{50}\delta/10^{10^{3000}}$.} \smallskip In this case we do not need to keep track of the condition that $L_t(v,w)\geqslant10$ because we have a very large gain in the quality of the new graph. The next stage of the argument is then:
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions
nodes.statement_short: Large quality gain: no need to track $L_t$.

nodes.name: Stage 3a
nodes.statement: {\it Stage 3a: Obtaining a GCD subgraph with} $\mathcal{R}(G^{(3\text{a})})=\emptyset$. \medskip Notice that if $H\preceq G^{(2)}$, then $\mathcal{R}(H)\subseteq\{p>10^{2000}\}$ by \eqref{eq:R of subgraphs}. Consequently, if $\mathcal{R}(H)\neq\emptyset$, then either Proposition \ref{prop:IterationStep1} or Proposition \ref{prop:IterationStep2} is applicable to $H$, thus producing a GCD subgraph $H'$ of $H$ such that \begin{equation} \mathcal{R}(H')\subsetneq \mathcal{R}(H) \quad\text{and}\quad q(H')\geqslant q(H). \end{equation} Since $\mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})$ is finite, starting with $H_1=G^{(2)}$ and iterating the above fact, we can construct a finite sequence of GCD subgraphs \[ G^{(2)}=H_1\succeq H_2\succeq\cdots\succeq H_J=:G^{(3\text{a})} \] such that \[ \mathcal{R}(G^{(3\text{a})})=\emptyset \quad \text{and}\quad q(G^{(3\text{a})})\geqslant q(G^{(2)}). \] Applying the assumption that $q(G^{(2)})/q(G)\geqslant (t/10)^{50}\delta/10^{10^{3000}}$, we infer that \[ q(G^{(3\text{a})})\geqslant \Bigl(\frac{t}{10}\Bigr)^{50}\frac{\delta}{10^{10^{3000}}} \cdot q(G). \] Hence, the GCD graph $G'=G^{(3\text{a})}$ satisfies condition \ref{prop:Parta} and condition \ref{prop:Partd}-\ref{prop:Case1} of Proposition \ref{prop:BoundOnEdges}, giving the result in this case. (Recall that we may also guarantee conditions \ref{prop:Partb} and \ref{prop:Partc} of Proposition \ref{prop:BoundOnEdges} by feeding our graph into Lemma \ref{lem:HighDegreeSubgraph}.)
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions

nodes.name: Iteration step
nodes.statement: {\it Stage 3a: Obtaining a GCD subgraph with} $\mathcal{R}(G^{(3\text{a})})=\emptyset$. \medskip Notice that if $H\preceq G^{(2)}$, then $\mathcal{R}(H)\subseteq\{p>10^{2000}\}$ by \eqref{eq:R of subgraphs}. Consequently, if $\mathcal{R}(H)\neq\emptyset$, then either Proposition \ref{prop:IterationStep1} or Proposition \ref{prop:IterationStep2} is applicable to $H$, thus producing a GCD subgraph $H'$ of $H$ such that \begin{equation} \mathcal{R}(H')\subsetneq \mathcal{R}(H) \quad\text{and}\quad q(H')\geqslant q(H). \end{equation}
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions

nodes.name: Iterate
nodes.statement: Since $\mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})$ is finite, starting with $H_1=G^{(2)}$ and iterating the above fact, we can construct a finite sequence of GCD subgraphs \[ G^{(2)}=H_1\succeq H_2\succeq\cdots\succeq H_J=:G^{(3\text{a})} \] such that \[ \mathcal{R}(G^{(3\text{a})})=\emptyset \quad \text{and}\quad q(G^{(3\text{a})})\geqslant q(G^{(2)}). \]
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions

nodes.name: Quality gain
nodes.statement: Applying the assumption that $q(G^{(2)})/q(G)\geqslant (t/10)^{50}\delta/10^{10^{3000}}$, we infer that \[ q(G^{(3\text{a})})\geqslant \Bigl(\frac{t}{10}\Bigr)^{50}\frac{\delta}{10^{10^{3000}}} \cdot q(G). \]
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions

nodes.name: Case (a) done
nodes.statement: Hence, the GCD graph $G'=G^{(3\text{a})}$ satisfies condition \ref{prop:Parta} and condition \ref{prop:Partd}-\ref{prop:Case1} of Proposition \ref{prop:BoundOnEdges}, giving the result in this case. (Recall that we may also guarantee conditions \ref{prop:Partb} and \ref{prop:Partc} of Proposition \ref{prop:BoundOnEdges} by feeding our graph into Lemma \ref{lem:HighDegreeSubgraph}.)
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions

nodes.name: Remaining case
nodes.statement: In order to complete the proof of Proposition \ref{prop:BoundOnEdges}, it remains to consider the situation when $q(G^{(2)})/q(G)$ is not large.
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions
nodes.statement_short: It remains to treat small quality gain.

nodes.name: Case (b): small gain
nodes.statement: {\it Case (b): $q(G^{(2)})/q(G)<(t/10)^{50}\delta/10^{10^{3000}}$.} \medskip In this case, the quality increment is small and we must make sure not to lose track of the condition $L_t(v,w)\geqslant10$. For this reason, we perform some cosmetic surgery to our graph before applying Proposition \ref{prop:IterationStep2}. This consists of {\it Stage 3b} that we present below.
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions
nodes.statement_short: Small gain: perform cosmetic surgery first.

nodes.name: Stage 3b: cosmetic surgery
nodes.statement:
{\it Stage 3b: Removing the effect of primes in $\mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})$ from the anatomical condition $L_t(v,w)\geqslant10$.} \medskip Note that \eqref{eq:G2Quality} implies that \[ \delta^{(2)}\geqslant rac{\delta}{10^{10^{3000}}} \cdot  rac {q(G)}{q(G^{(2)})}\geqslant \Bigl( rac{10}{t}\Bigr)^{50}, \] and that \eq{ 2^N\leqslant 10^{10^{3000}} \cdot  rac{q(G^{(2)})}{q(G)}\leqslant \Bigl( rac{t}{10}\Bigr)^{50}\delta\leqslant t^{50}, } where we recall that \[ N=\#\{p\in\mathcal{P}^{(2)}\setminus\mathcal{P}^{(1)}:f^{(2)}(p)
e g^{(2)}(p)\} \] (here we used the trivial bound $\delta\leqslant 1$). Since $\delta^{(2)}\geqslant (10/t)^{50}$, $\mathcal{R}^ lat(G^{(2)})=\emptyset$, and $L_t(v,w)\geqslant10$ for all $(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}^{(2)}$, it is the case that $G^{(2)}$ satisfies the conditions of Lemma ef{lem:Cosmetic}. Consequently, there exists a GCD subgraph $G^{(3	ext{b})}=(\mu,\mathcal{V}^{(3	ext{b})},\mathcal{W}^{(3	ext{b})},\mathcal{E}^{(3	ext{b})},\mathcal{P}^{(3	ext{b})},f^{(3	ext{b})},g^{(3	ext{b})})$ of $G^{(2)}$ with  egin{align} \mathcal{P}^{(3	ext{b})}&=\mathcal{P}^{(2)},\ q(G^{(3	ext{b})})&\geqslant  rac{q(G^{(2)})}{2}, \end{align} and such that  egin{equation} \sum_{\substack{p|v w/\gcd(v,w)^2\p\geqslant t,\ p
otin \mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})}} rac{1}{p}\geqslant 5 \quad	ext{whenever}\quad (v,w)\in\mathcal{E}^{(3	ext{b})}, \end{equation} We claim that an inequality of the form \eqref{eq:Anat1} holds even if we remove from consideration the primes lying in the set \[ \mathcal{P}^{(2)}_{	ext{diff}}:=\{p\in\mathcal{P}^{(2)}:\,f^{(2)}(p)
e g^{(2)}(p)\}. \] It turns out that we can do this rather crudely, starting from the estimate \[ \sum_{\substack{p|v w/\gcd(v,w)^2\p\geqslant t,\ p\in \mathcal{P}^{(2)}_{	ext{diff}}}} rac{1}{p} \leqslant  rac{\#(\mathcal{P}_{	ext{diff}}^{(2)}\cap\{p\geqslant t\})}{t}. \] Recalling that $t>10^{2000}$ and $\mathcal{P}^{(1)}\subseteq\{p\leqslant10^{2000}\}$, we deduce that  egin{equation} \sum_{\substack{p|v w/\gcd(v,w)^2\p\geqslant t,\ p\in \mathcal{P}^{(2)}_{	ext{diff}}}} rac{1}{p} \leqslant  rac{\#(\mathcal{P}_{	ext{diff}}^{(2)}\setminus\mathcal{P}^{(1)} )}{t}= rac{N}{t}. \end{equation} Since $t\geqslant 10^{2000}$, relation \eqref{eq:N-bound} implies that $N\leqslant 2\log(t^{50})=100\log t<t$, that is to say the right hand side of \eqref{eq:removing P^2_diff} is $\leqslant 1$. As a consequence,  egin{equation} \sum_{\substack{p|v w/\gcd(v,w)^2\ p\geqslant t,\ p
otin \mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})\cup \mathcal{P}^{(2)}_{	ext{diff}}}} rac{1}{p}\geqslant 4 \quad	ext{whenever}\quad (v,w)\in\mathcal{E}^{(3	ext{b})}. \end{equation} Having removed the effect to the condition $L_t(v,w)\geqslant10$ of primes from the sets $\mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})\cup\mathcal{P}_{	ext{diff}}^{(2)}$, we are ready to complete the construction of $G'$ in Case (b).
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 8.4 removes the influence of $\mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})$ and $\mathcal{P}_{\rm diff}$ on $L_t$.

nodes.name: Density and N bounds
nodes.statement: {\it Stage 3b: Removing the effect of primes in $\mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})$ from the anatomical condition $L_t(v,w)\geqslant10$.} \medskip Note that \eqref{eq:G2Quality} implies that \[ \delta^{(2)}\geqslant\frac{\delta}{10^{10^{3000}}} \cdot \frac {q(G)}{q(G^{(2)})}\geqslant \Bigl(\frac{10}{t}\Bigr)^{50}, \] and that \eq{ 2^N\leqslant 10^{10^{3000}} \cdot \frac{q(G^{(2)})}{q(G)}\leqslant \Bigl(\frac{t}{10}\Bigr)^{50}\delta\leqslant t^{50}, } where we recall that \[ N=\#\{p\in\mathcal{P}^{(2)}\setminus\mathcal{P}^{(1)}:f^{(2)}(p)\ne g^{(2)}(p)\} \] (here we used the trivial bound $\delta\leqslant 1$).
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 8.4
nodes.statement: Since $\delta^{(2)}\geqslant (10/t)^{50}$, $\mathcal{R}^\flat(G^{(2)})=\emptyset$, and $L_t(v,w)\geqslant10$ for all $(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}^{(2)}$, it is the case that $G^{(2)}$ satisfies the conditions of Lemma \ref{lem:Cosmetic}. Consequently, there exists a GCD subgraph $G^{(3\text{b})}=(\mu,\mathcal{V}^{(3\text{b})},\mathcal{W}^{(3\text{b})},\mathcal{E}^{(3\text{b})},\mathcal{P}^{(3\text{b})},f^{(3\text{b})},g^{(3\text{b})})$ of $G^{(2)}$ with \begin{align} \mathcal{P}^{(3\text{b})}&=\mathcal{P}^{(2)},\\ q(G^{(3\text{b})})&\geqslant \frac{q(G^{(2)})}{2}, \end{align} and such that \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{p|v w/\gcd(v,w)^2\\p\geqslant t,\ p\notin \mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})}}\frac{1}{p}\geqslant 5 \quad\text{whenever}\quad (v,w)\in\mathcal{E}^{(3\text{b})}, \end{equation}
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 8.4 gives $G^{(3b)}$ with prime sum $\ge5$ outside $\mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})$.

nodes.name: Remove P_diff
nodes.statement: We claim that an inequality of the form \eqref{eq:Anat1} holds even if we remove from consideration the primes lying in the set \[ \mathcal{P}^{(2)}_{\text{diff}}:=\{p\in\mathcal{P}^{(2)}:\,f^{(2)}(p)\ne g^{(2)}(p)\}. \] It turns out that we can do this rather crudely, starting from the estimate \[ \sum_{\substack{p|v w/\gcd(v,w)^2\\p\geqslant t,\ p\in \mathcal{P}^{(2)}_{\text{diff}}}}\frac{1}{p} \leqslant \frac{\#(\mathcal{P}_{\text{diff}}^{(2)}\cap\{p\geqslant t\})}{t}. \] Recalling that $t>10^{2000}$ and $\mathcal{P}^{(1)}\subseteq\{p\leqslant10^{2000}\}$, we deduce that \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{p|v w/\gcd(v,w)^2\\p\geqslant t,\ p\in \mathcal{P}^{(2)}_{\text{diff}}}}\frac{1}{p} \leqslant \frac{\#(\mathcal{P}_{\text{diff}}^{(2)}\setminus\mathcal{P}^{(1)} )}{t}=\frac{N}{t}. \end{equation} Since $t\geqslant 10^{2000}$, relation \eqref{eq:N-bound} implies that $N\leqslant 2\log(t^{50})=100\log t<t$, that is to say the right hand side of \eqref{eq:removing P^2_diff} is $\leqslant 1$. As a consequence, \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{p|v w/\gcd(v,w)^2\\ p\geqslant t,\ p\notin \mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})\cup \mathcal{P}^{(2)}_{\text{diff}}}}\frac{1}{p}\geqslant 4 \quad\text{whenever}\quad (v,w)\in\mathcal{E}^{(3\text{b})}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions

nodes.name: State claim
nodes.statement: We claim that an inequality of the form \eqref{eq:Anat1} holds even if we remove from consideration the primes lying in the set \[ \mathcal{P}^{(2)}_{\text{diff}}:=\{p\in\mathcal{P}^{(2)}:\,f^{(2)}(p)\ne g^{(2)}(p)\}. \]
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions

nodes.name: Crude bound
nodes.statement: It turns out that we can do this rather crudely, starting from the estimate \[ \sum_{\substack{p|v w/\gcd(v,w)^2\\p\geqslant t,\ p\in \mathcal{P}^{(2)}_{\text{diff}}}}\frac{1}{p} \leqslant \frac{\#(\mathcal{P}_{\text{diff}}^{(2)}\cap\{p\geqslant t\})}{t}. \]
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions
nodes.statement_short: Bound the $\mathcal{P}_{\rm diff}$ contribution by count over $t$.

nodes.name: Count is N
nodes.statement: Recalling that $t>10^{2000}$ and $\mathcal{P}^{(1)}\subseteq\{p\leqslant10^{2000}\}$, we deduce that \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{p|v w/\gcd(v,w)^2\\p\geqslant t,\ p\in \mathcal{P}^{(2)}_{\text{diff}}}}\frac{1}{p} \leqslant \frac{\#(\mathcal{P}_{\text{diff}}^{(2)}\setminus\mathcal{P}^{(1)} )}{t}=\frac{N}{t}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions

nodes.name: N < t
nodes.statement: Since $t\geqslant 10^{2000}$, relation \eqref{eq:N-bound} implies that $N\leqslant 2\log(t^{50})=100\log t<t$, that is to say the right hand side of \eqref{eq:removing P^2_diff} is $\leqslant 1$. As a consequence, \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{p|v w/\gcd(v,w)^2\\ p\geqslant t,\ p\notin \mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})\cup \mathcal{P}^{(2)}_{\text{diff}}}}\frac{1}{p}\geqslant 4 \quad\text{whenever}\quad (v,w)\in\mathcal{E}^{(3\text{b})}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions

nodes.name: Transition
nodes.statement: Having removed the effect to the condition $L_t(v,w)\geqslant10$ of primes from the sets $\mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})\cup\mathcal{P}_{\text{diff}}^{(2)}$, we are ready to complete the construction of $G'$ in Case (b).
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions

nodes.name: Stage 4b
nodes.statement:
{\it Stage 4b: Obtaining a GCD subgraph with} $\mathcal{R}(G^{(4	ext{b})})=\emptyset$. \medskip We argue as in Stage 3a: for each $H\preceq G^{(3	ext{b})}$, we have $\mathcal{R}(H)\subseteq\{p>10^{2000}\}$ by \eqref{eq:R of subgraphs}. Hence, if $\mathcal{R}(H)
eq\emptyset$, then either Proposition ef{prop:IterationStep1} or Proposition ef{prop:IterationStep2} is applicable to $H$, thus producing a GCD subgraph $H'$ of $H$ such that  egin{equation} \mathcal{R}(H')\subsetneq \mathcal{R}(H),\quad \mathcal{P}_{H'}\subseteq \mathcal{R}(H)\cup \mathcal{P}_H , \quad	ext{and}\quad q(H')\geqslant q(H), \end{equation} where $\mathcal{P}_H$ and $\mathcal{P}_{H'}$ denote the set of primes of $H$ and of $H'$, respectively. Since $\mathcal{R}(G^{(3	ext{b})})$ is finite, starting with $H_1=G^{(3	ext{b})}$ and iterating the above fact, we can construct a finite sequence of GCD subgraphs \[ G^{(3	ext{b})}=H_1\succeq H_2\succeq\cdots\succeq H_J=:G^{(4	ext{b})} \] such that \[ \mathcal{R}(G^{(4	ext{b})})=\emptyset\quad	ext{and}\quad q(G^{(4	ext{b})})\geqslant q(G^{(3	ext{b})}). \] In addition, note that \[ \mathcal{P}^{(4	ext{b})} \subseteq \mathcal{R}(G^{(3	ext{b})})\cup\mathcal{P}^{(3	ext{b})} \subseteq \mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})\cup\mathcal{P}^{(2)}, \] where the second relation follows by fact \eqref{eq:P3b} that $\mathcal{P}^{(3	ext{b})}=\mathcal{P}^{(2)}$. We now verify that if we let \[ G'=G^{(4b)}, \] then condition ef{prop:Partd}-ef{prop:Case2} of Proposition ef{prop:BoundOnEdges} is satisfied. This suffices for the completion of the proof, since $G'$ clearly satisfies condition ef{prop:Parta} of Proposition ef{prop:BoundOnEdges}, and an application of Lemma ef{lem:HighDegreeSubgraph} can also ensure conditions ef{prop:Partb} and ef{prop:Partc}. First of all, note that by \eqref{eq:G3Quality} and \eqref{eq:G2Quality} and $q(G^{(4	ext{b})})\geqslant q(G^{(3	ext{b})})$, we have \[ q(G') = q(G^{(4	ext{b})})\geqslant q(G^{(3	ext{b})})\geqslant  rac{q(G^{(2)})}{2} \geqslant  rac{q(G)}{2\cdot 10^{10^{3000}}}. \] Let $(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}^{(4	ext{b})}$. It remains to check that $L_t(v',w')\geqslant4$, where $v'$ and $w'$ are defined by the relations \[ v=v'\prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}^{(4	ext{b})}}p^{f^{(4	ext{b})}(p)} \quad	ext{and}\quad w=w'\prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}^{(4	ext{b})}}p^{g^{(4	ext{b})}(p)}. \] By the definition of the set $\mathcal{R}(G^{(4	ext{b})})$ and since $\mathcal{R}(G^{(4b)})=\emptyset$, all prime factors of $\gcd(v,w)$ belong to $\mathcal{P}^{(4	ext{b})}$. But for each prime $p\in\mathcal{P}^{(4	ext{b})}$ we have $p^{\min\{f^{(4	ext{b})}(p),g^{(4	ext{b})}(p)\}}\|\gcd(v,w)$. Thus \[ \gcd(v,w) = \prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}^{(4	ext{b})}}p^{\min\{f^{(4	ext{b})}(p),g^{(4	ext{b})}(p)\}}. \] In particular, we must have that \[ \gcd(v',w')=1. \] Now, let $p$ be a prime such that \[ p| rac{vw}{\gcd(v,w)^2}\quad	ext{and}\quad p
mid v'w'. \] Since $p
mid v'w'$ but $p|vw$, we must have $p\in\mathcal{P}^{(4	ext{b})}$, and so $p^{\min\{f^{(4	ext{b})}(p),g^{(4	ext{b})}(p)\}}\|\gcd(v,w)$. In addition, our assumptions that $p
mid v'w'$ and $p|v w/\gcd(v,w)^2$ imply that $f^{(4	ext{b})}(p)
e g^{(4	ext{b})}(p)$. If $p\in\mathcal{P}^{(2)}$, we infer that $p\in \mathcal{P}^{(2)}_{	ext{diff}}$. On the other hand, if $p
otin\mathcal{P}^{(2)}$, then the inclusion $\mathcal{P}^{(4	ext{b})}\subseteq \mathcal{P}^{(2)}\cup\mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})$ implies that $p\in \mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})$. In either case, we have that $p\in\mathcal{P}^{(2)}_{	ext{diff}}\cup\mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})$. Thus, since $\mathcal{E}^{(4	ext{b})}\subseteq\mathcal{E}^{(3	ext{b})}$, we may use the bound \eqref{eq:Anat4}, which gives \[ L_t(v',w')=\sum_{\substack{p|v' w'/\gcd(v',w')^2\ p\geqslant t}} rac{1}{p}\geqslant\sum_{\substack{p|v w/\gcd(v,w)^2\p\geqslant t,\ p
otin \mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})\cup \mathcal{P}^{(2)}_{	ext{diff}}}} rac{1}{p}\geqslant 4. \] In particular, $G'=G^{(4	ext{b})}$ satisfies the conditions of case ef{prop:Partd}-ef{prop:Case2} of Proposition ef{prop:BoundOnEdges}. This completes the proof of Proposition ef{prop:BoundOnEdges} in Case (b) too.
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions
nodes.statement_short: Iterate Props. 8.1/8.2 to empty $\mathcal{R}$ and verify (d)(ii).

nodes.name: Iteration step
nodes.statement: {\it Stage 4b: Obtaining a GCD subgraph with} $\mathcal{R}(G^{(4\text{b})})=\emptyset$. \medskip We argue as in Stage 3a: for each $H\preceq G^{(3\text{b})}$, we have $\mathcal{R}(H)\subseteq\{p>10^{2000}\}$ by \eqref{eq:R of subgraphs}. Hence, if $\mathcal{R}(H)\neq\emptyset$, then either Proposition \ref{prop:IterationStep1} or Proposition \ref{prop:IterationStep2} is applicable to $H$, thus producing a GCD subgraph $H'$ of $H$ such that \begin{equation} \mathcal{R}(H')\subsetneq \mathcal{R}(H),\quad \mathcal{P}_{H'}\subseteq \mathcal{R}(H)\cup \mathcal{P}_H , \quad\text{and}\quad q(H')\geqslant q(H), \end{equation} where $\mathcal{P}_H$ and $\mathcal{P}_{H'}$ denote the set of primes of $H$ and of $H'$, respectively.
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions
nodes.statement_short: Each step shrinks $\mathcal{R}$ without quality loss.

nodes.name: Iterate
nodes.statement: Since $\mathcal{R}(G^{(3\text{b})})$ is finite, starting with $H_1=G^{(3\text{b})}$ and iterating the above fact, we can construct a finite sequence of GCD subgraphs \[ G^{(3\text{b})}=H_1\succeq H_2\succeq\cdots\succeq H_J=:G^{(4\text{b})} \] such that \[ \mathcal{R}(G^{(4\text{b})})=\emptyset\quad\text{and}\quad q(G^{(4\text{b})})\geqslant q(G^{(3\text{b})}). \]
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions

nodes.name: Prime set inclusion
nodes.statement: In addition, note that \[ \mathcal{P}^{(4\text{b})} \subseteq \mathcal{R}(G^{(3\text{b})})\cup\mathcal{P}^{(3\text{b})} \subseteq \mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})\cup\mathcal{P}^{(2)}, \] where the second relation follows by fact \eqref{eq:P3b} that $\mathcal{P}^{(3\text{b})}=\mathcal{P}^{(2)}$.
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions

nodes.name: Verify (d)(ii)
nodes.statement: We now verify that if we let \[ G'=G^{(4b)}, \] then condition \ref{prop:Partd}-\ref{prop:Case2} of Proposition \ref{prop:BoundOnEdges} is satisfied. This suffices for the completion of the proof, since $G'$ clearly satisfies condition \ref{prop:Parta} of Proposition \ref{prop:BoundOnEdges}, and an application of Lemma \ref{lem:HighDegreeSubgraph} can also ensure conditions \ref{prop:Partb} and \ref{prop:Partc}.
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions

nodes.name: Quality bound
nodes.statement: First of all, note that by \eqref{eq:G3Quality} and \eqref{eq:G2Quality} and $q(G^{(4\text{b})})\geqslant q(G^{(3\text{b})})$, we have \[ q(G') = q(G^{(4\text{b})})\geqslant q(G^{(3\text{b})})\geqslant \frac{q(G^{(2)})}{2} \geqslant \frac{q(G)}{2\cdot 10^{10^{3000}}}. \]
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions

nodes.name: Define v', w'
nodes.statement: Let $(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}^{(4\text{b})}$. It remains to check that $L_t(v',w')\geqslant4$, where $v'$ and $w'$ are defined by the relations \[ v=v'\prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}^{(4\text{b})}}p^{f^{(4\text{b})}(p)} \quad\text{and}\quad w=w'\prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}^{(4\text{b})}}p^{g^{(4\text{b})}(p)}. \]
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions

nodes.name: gcd(v',w')=1
nodes.statement: By the definition of the set $\mathcal{R}(G^{(4\text{b})})$ and since $\mathcal{R}(G^{(4b)})=\emptyset$, all prime factors of $\gcd(v,w)$ belong to $\mathcal{P}^{(4\text{b})}$. But for each prime $p\in\mathcal{P}^{(4\text{b})}$ we have $p^{\min\{f^{(4\text{b})}(p),g^{(4\text{b})}(p)\}}\|\gcd(v,w)$. Thus \[ \gcd(v,w) = \prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}^{(4\text{b})}}p^{\min\{f^{(4\text{b})}(p),g^{(4\text{b})}(p)\}}. \] In particular, we must have that \[ \gcd(v',w')=1. \]
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions
nodes.statement_short: All gcd primes lie in $\mathcal{P}^{(4b)}$, so $\gcd(v',w')=1$.

nodes.name: Lost primes
nodes.statement:
Now, let $p$ be a prime such that \[ p| rac{vw}{\gcd(v,w)^2}\quad	ext{and}\quad p
mid v'w'. \] Since $p
mid v'w'$ but $p|vw$, we must have $p\in\mathcal{P}^{(4	ext{b})}$, and so $p^{\min\{f^{(4	ext{b})}(p),g^{(4	ext{b})}(p)\}}\|\gcd(v,w)$. In addition, our assumptions that $p
mid v'w'$ and $p|v w/\gcd(v,w)^2$ imply that $f^{(4	ext{b})}(p)
e g^{(4	ext{b})}(p)$.
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions
nodes.statement_short: A prime lost from $vw/\gcd^2$ has $f\ne g$.

nodes.name: Lost primes are excluded
nodes.statement: If $p\in\mathcal{P}^{(2)}$, we infer that $p\in \mathcal{P}^{(2)}_{\text{diff}}$. On the other hand, if $p\notin\mathcal{P}^{(2)}$, then the inclusion $\mathcal{P}^{(4\text{b})}\subseteq \mathcal{P}^{(2)}\cup\mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})$ implies that $p\in \mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})$. In either case, we have that $p\in\mathcal{P}^{(2)}_{\text{diff}}\cup\mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})$. Thus, since $\mathcal{E}^{(4\text{b})}\subseteq\mathcal{E}^{(3\text{b})}$, we may use the bound \eqref{eq:Anat4}, which gives \[ L_t(v',w')=\sum_{\substack{p|v' w'/\gcd(v',w')^2\\ p\geqslant t}}\frac{1}{p}\geqslant\sum_{\substack{p|v w/\gcd(v,w)^2\\p\geqslant t,\ p\notin \mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})\cup \mathcal{P}^{(2)}_{\text{diff}}}}\frac{1}{p}\geqslant 4. \]
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions
nodes.statement_short: Such primes lie in $\mathcal{P}_{\rm diff}\cup\mathcal{R}(G^{(2)})$, so (8.9) gives $L_t(v',w')\ge4$.

nodes.name: Case (b) done
nodes.statement: In particular, $G'=G^{(4\text{b})}$ satisfies the conditions of case \ref{prop:Partd}-\ref{prop:Case2} of Proposition \ref{prop:BoundOnEdges}. This completes the proof of Proposition \ref{prop:BoundOnEdges} in Case (b) too.
nodes.section: 8 Reduction of Proposition 7.1 to three iterative propositions

nodes.name: Define S(v,w)
nodes.statement: In this section we establish Lemma \ref{lem:Cosmetic} directly. For brevity, let \[ S(v,w) = \sum_{\substack{p|v w/\gcd(v,w)^2\\p\in \mathcal{R}(G),\ p\geqslant t^{50}}}\frac{1}{p}. \]

nodes.name: Swap sums
nodes.statement: We have \[ \sum_{(v,w)\in\mathcal{E} } \mu(v)\mu(w) S(v,w) = \sum_{\substack{p\in \mathcal{R}(G) \\ p\geqslant t^{50}}}\frac{1}{p}\cdot \mu\Bigl(\Bigl\{(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}: p|\frac{v w}{\gcd(v,w)^2}\Bigr\}\Bigr) . \]
nodes.statement_short: Swap the order of summation over edges and primes.

nodes.name: p in R-sharp
nodes.statement: Fix for the moment a prime $p\in\mathcal{R}(G)$. Since we have $\mathcal{R}^\flat(G)=\emptyset$, it must be the case that $p\in\mathcal{R}^\sharp(G)$, that is to say there exists some $k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geqslant0}$ such that \[ \mu(\mathcal{V}_{p^k})\geqslant\Bigl(1-\frac{10^{40}}{p}\Bigr)\mu(\mathcal{V}) \quad\text{and}\quad \mu(\mathcal{W}_{p^k})\geqslant\Bigl(1-\frac{10^{40}}{p}\Bigr)\mu(\mathcal{W}). \]

nodes.name: Unbalanced edges are few
nodes.statement: Now we note that if $p|v w/\gcd(v,w)^2$, then $p^j\|v$ and $p^\ell\|w$ for some $j\ne \ell$. In particular we cannot have $p^k \|v$ and $p^k\|w$. Thus \als{ \mu\Bigl(\Bigl\{(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}: p|\frac{v w}{\gcd(v,w)^2}\Bigr\}\Bigr)&\leqslant \mu((\mathcal{V}\setminus\mathcal{V}_{p^k})\times \mathcal{W})+\mu(\mathcal{V}\times( \mathcal{W}\setminus\mathcal{W}_{p^k}))\\ & \leqslant 2\cdot \frac{10^{40}}{p} \cdot \mu(\mathcal{V})\mu(\mathcal{W}) . }

nodes.name: First moment bound
nodes.statement: Thus we conclude that \als{ \sum_{(v,w)\in\mathcal{E} } \mu(v)\mu(w) S(v,w) &\leqslant \sum_{p\geqslant t^{50}}\frac{2\cdot 10^{40} \mu(\mathcal{V})\mu(\mathcal{W}) }{p^2}\\ &\leqslant \frac{2\cdot 10^{40}\mu(\mathcal{V})\mu(\mathcal{W}) }{t^{50}}\\ &<\frac{\mu(\mathcal{E}) } {100}, } where in the final line we used the fact that $\delta=\mu(\mathcal{E})/\mu(\mathcal{V})\mu(\mathcal{W})\geqslant (10/t)^{50}$.

nodes.name: Prune edges
nodes.statement: Now, let us define \[ \mathcal{E}':=\{(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}: S(v,w)\leqslant 1\}. \] Evidently, we have that \[ \mu(\mathcal{E}\setminus\mathcal{E}')=\sum_{\substack{(v,w)\in\mathcal{E} \\ S(v,w)>1}}\mu(v)\mu(w)\leqslant \sum_{(v,w)\in\mathcal{E} } \mu(v)\mu(w) S(v,w) <\frac{\mu(\mathcal{E})}{100}. \] Thus $\mu(\mathcal{E}')\geqslant 99\mu(\mathcal{E})/100$. We then take $G':=(\mu,\mathcal{V},\mathcal{W},\mathcal{E}',\mathcal{P},f,g)$ and note that \[ \frac{q(G')}{q(G)}=\Bigl(\frac{\mu(\mathcal{E}')}{\mu(\mathcal{E})}\Bigr)^{10}\geqslant \frac{1}{2} . \]
nodes.statement_short: Drop edges with $S>1$; quality drops by at most half.

nodes.name: Mertens on [t,t^50]
nodes.statement: Finally, we note that \[ \sum_{t\leqslant p\leqslant t^{50}}\frac{1}{p}= \lim_{y\to t^-}\sum_{y<p\leqslant t^{50}}\frac{1}{p}\leqslant \log(50)+\frac{1}{(\log t)^2} \leqslant 4 \] for $t\geqslant 300$ by \cite[Theorem 5]{RS}, and so if $(v',w')\in\mathcal{E}'$ then \[ \sum_{\substack{p|v' w'/\gcd(v',w')^2\\p\in \mathcal{R}(G)\\ p\geqslant t}}\frac{1}{p}\leqslant \sum_{\substack{p|v' w'/\gcd(v',w')^2\\p\in \mathcal{R}(G)\\ p\geqslant t^{50}}}\frac{1}{p}+4\leqslant 5. \]

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Hence, since $\mathcal{E}'\subseteq\mathcal{E}\subseteq \{(v,w)\in \mathcal{V}\times\mathcal{W}: L_t(v,w)\geqslant 10\}$, for any $(v',w')\in\mathcal{E}'$ we have \[ \sum_{\substack{p|v' w'/\gcd(v',w')^2\\p\notin \mathcal{R}(G)\\ p\geqslant t}}\frac{1}{p}\geqslant L_t(v',w')-5\geqslant 5. \] This completes the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:Cosmetic}.\qed

nodes.name: Low-degree vertex
nodes.statement: Assume that (a) fails. Then either its first or its second inequality fails. Assume that the first one fails for some $v\in\mathcal{V}$; the other case is entirely analogous.

nodes.name: Delete v
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{E}'$ be the set of edges between the vertex sets $\mathcal{V}\setminus\{v\}$ and $\mathcal{W}$. Note that \[ \mu(\mathcal{E}')= \mu(\mathcal{E})-\mu(v)\mu(\Gamma_G(v)) >0 \] because $\mu(\Gamma_G(v))<9\delta\mu(\mathcal{W})/10$, $\mu(v)\leqslant \mu(\mathcal{V})$, and $\mu(\mathcal{E})>0$ by the assumption $\delta>0$. In particular, we have $\mu(\mathcal{W}),\mu(\mathcal{V}\setminus\{v\})>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Remove $v$; the remaining edge measure is positive.

nodes.name: Subgraph G'
nodes.statement: We then consider $G'=(\mu,\mathcal{V}\setminus\{v\},\mathcal{W},\mathcal{E}',\mathcal{P},f,g)$, which is a GCD subgraph of $G$. Let $G'$ have edge density $\delta'$.

nodes.name: Claim no loss
nodes.statement: We claim that $\delta'\geqslant \delta$ and $q(G')\geqslant q(G)$. Indeed, we have \als{ \mu(\mathcal{E}') = \mu(\mathcal{E})-\mu(v)\mu(\Gamma_G(v)) &\geqslant \delta \mu(\mathcal{V})\mu(\mathcal{W})-\frac{9\delta}{10}\mu(v)\mu(\mathcal{W}) \\ &=\delta \big(\mu(\mathcal{V})-\mu(v)\big)\mu(\mathcal{W})\cdot\Big(1+\frac{\mu(v)/10}{\mu(\mathcal{V})-\mu(v)}\Big). } Thus the edge density $\delta'$ of $G'$ satisfies \[ \delta'=\frac{\mu(\mathcal{E}')}{\mu(\mathcal{V}\setminus\{v\})\mu(\mathcal{W})} =\frac{\mu(\mathcal{E}')}{\big(\mu(\mathcal{V})-\mu(v)\big)\mu(\mathcal{W})} \geqslant \delta\cdot \Bigl(1+\frac{\mu(v)/10}{\mu(\mathcal{V})-\mu(v)}\Bigr). \] Thus we see that $\delta'\geqslant \delta$, and that \begin{align*} (\delta')^{10}\mu(\mathcal{V}\setminus\{v\})\mu(\mathcal{W}) &\geqslant \delta^{10}\big(\mu(\mathcal{V})-\mu(v)\big)\mu(\mathcal{W}) \Bigl(1+\frac{\mu(v)}{\mu(\mathcal{V})-\mu(v)}\Bigr) = \delta^{10} \mu(\mathcal{V})\mu(\mathcal{W}) . \end{align*} This proves our claim that $q(G')\geqslant q(G)$ too, thus completing the proof of the lemma.

nodes.name: State claim
nodes.statement: We claim that $\delta'\geqslant \delta$ and $q(G')\geqslant q(G)$.
nodes.statement_short: Claim density and quality do not drop.

nodes.name: Edge measure bound
nodes.statement: Indeed, we have \als{ \mu(\mathcal{E}') = \mu(\mathcal{E})-\mu(v)\mu(\Gamma_G(v)) &\geqslant \delta \mu(\mathcal{V})\mu(\mathcal{W})-\frac{9\delta}{10}\mu(v)\mu(\mathcal{W}) \\ &=\delta \big(\mu(\mathcal{V})-\mu(v)\big)\mu(\mathcal{W})\cdot\Big(1+\frac{\mu(v)/10}{\mu(\mathcal{V})-\mu(v)}\Big). }

nodes.name: Density bound
nodes.statement: Thus the edge density $\delta'$ of $G'$ satisfies \[ \delta'=\frac{\mu(\mathcal{E}')}{\mu(\mathcal{V}\setminus\{v\})\mu(\mathcal{W})} =\frac{\mu(\mathcal{E}')}{\big(\mu(\mathcal{V})-\mu(v)\big)\mu(\mathcal{W})} \geqslant \delta\cdot \Bigl(1+\frac{\mu(v)/10}{\mu(\mathcal{V})-\mu(v)}\Bigr). \]

nodes.name: Quality bound
nodes.statement: Thus we see that $\delta'\geqslant \delta$, and that \begin{align*} (\delta')^{10}\mu(\mathcal{V}\setminus\{v\})\mu(\mathcal{W}) &\geqslant \delta^{10}\big(\mu(\mathcal{V})-\mu(v)\big)\mu(\mathcal{W}) \Bigl(1+\frac{\mu(v)}{\mu(\mathcal{V})-\mu(v)}\Bigr) = \delta^{10} \mu(\mathcal{V})\mu(\mathcal{W}) . \end{align*} This proves our claim that $q(G')\geqslant q(G)$ too, thus completing the proof of the lemma.

nodes.name: Iterate Lemma 10.1
nodes.statement: We note that conclusion $(c)$ of Lemma \ref{lem:HighDegreeSubgraph} is the same as conclusion $(a)$ of Lemma \ref{lem:HighDegree}. Thus, if $G$ does not satisfy conclusion $(c)$ of Lemma \ref{lem:HighDegreeSubgraph}, then we may repeatedly apply Lemma \ref{lem:HighDegree} to produce a sequence of GCD subgraphs \[ G=:G_1\succeq G_2\succeq\cdots \] until we arrive at a GCD subgraph of $G$ which satisfies conclusion $(a)$ of Lemma \ref{lem:HighDegree}.

nodes.name: Termination
nodes.statement: This process must terminate after a finite number of steps since at least one of the vertex sets of $G_{i+1}$ has one less element than the corresponding vertex set of $G_i$.
nodes.statement_short: Vertex sets shrink, so the process stops.

nodes.name: Monotonicity
nodes.statement: Let the process terminate at $G_J$, which satisfies conclusion $(a)$ of Lemma \ref{lem:HighDegree}, and let $\delta_i$ be the edge density of $G_i$. Since $\delta_{i+1}\geqslant \delta_i$ and $q(G_{i+1})\geqslant q(G_i)$ by Lemma \ref{lem:HighDegree}, we have that \[ \delta_J\geqslant \delta_{J-1}\geqslant \dots \geqslant \delta_1=\delta,\quad \text{and}\quad q(G_J)\geqslant q(G_{J-1})\geqslant \dots\geqslant q(G_1)=q(G). \]

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Since the multiplicative data are also maintained at each iteration, we see that taking $G'=G_J$ gives the result.

nodes.name: Edge partition
nodes.statement: For brevity let $\mathcal{E}_{i,j}=\mathcal{E}\cap(\mathcal{V}_i\times\mathcal{W}_j)$ be the edges between $\mathcal{V}_i$ and $\mathcal{W}_j$ for $i\in\{1,\dots,I\}$ and $j\in \{1,\dots,J\}$.
